News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez and Alexis Mac Allister employ private security after Argentina’s heated World Cup win vs England
Sports.content:
LISANDRO MARTINEZ and Alexis Mac Allister had security on patrol at their houses after Argentina’s World Cup win against England.

Private security firms were on site at the north-west homes of the Manchester United defender and Liverpool midfielder.



Security personnel were present for two days with emotions high after England‘s 2-1 semi-final loss.

Argentina defender Martinez clutched a banner that read ‘The Falklands are Argentina’s’ while Mac Allister was nearby during celebrations with the bedsheet visible.



Cristian Romero and his former Tottenham teammate Giovani Lo Celso also held the sign aloft, but the wantaway Romero could leave Spurs this summer.

No attempts to vandalise Martinez’s or Mac Allister’s properties were made and United were not involved in arranging the security detail for Martinez’s residence.



A mural of Marcus Rashford in Withington, Manchester was defaced after he missed a penalty for England against Italy in the European Championship final in 2021.

Martinez has developed a cult following since he joined United in July 2022 and their matchgoers have chanted “Argentina” in support of their Argentinian players over the last 25 years.

After Argentina won the 2022 World Cup, United fans welcomed Martinez back to Old Trafford by unfurling an Argentina flag in the Stretford End.

Mac Allister’s success in 2022 was similarly celebrated by Brighton, his club at the time. Seagulls supporters made homemade banners in tribute to the Argentine.



United’s and Liverpool’s fanbases are renowned for their lack of enthusiasm concerning the England national team.

A ‘We’re not English, we’re Scouse’ banner is frequently seen at Liverpool matches while a ‘United>England’ banner is permanently pinned up at Old Trafford.

United fans started chanting ‘Argentina’ in solidarity with David Beckham after his red card against the South American side in the 1998 World Cup.

Sports.title: Brentford reveal new away kit inspired by Hollywood film as fans say ‘most aura-ful reveal I’ve ever seen’
Sports.content:
BRENTFORD have unveiled a blockbuster 2026/27 away kit, bringing Hollywood razzmatazz to West London.

Kingsman director and co-creator Sir Matthew Vaughn is a minority shareholder in the Premier League outfit.



And the club have taken full advantage of his silver screen credentials for a cinematic kit reveal of their own.

The renowned spy thriller franchise features razor-sharp style, and Brentford‘s launch video follows suit – literally.



A glitzy unveiling clip opens with star striker Igor Thiago decked out in a bespoke pinstripe two-piece, designed by H. Huntsman & Sons – the very same Saville Row tailor that serves as the Kingsman HQ.

In a kit reveal directed by Sir Matthew himself, Brentford’s dapper South American ace is also seen wielding the legendary Kingsman umbrella, before the suit fades into a football strip.

A midnight navy base is decked out with classy cream pinstripes and crew neck collar to round off the away day design.

Social media has gone into a frenzy over the distinctive reveal, with one punter going as far as to declare: “That’s the most aura-ful reveal I’ve ever seen.”

Fans lapped up the Hollywood stardust, asking: “If I wear it, do I get a secret gadget and a license to score?”

Another quipped: “Some people [are] about to go to job interviews and weddings wearing this.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Self-professed Kingsman fanatic Igor Thiago also felt the kit was yet “another example of how Brentford always does something new and interesting.”

Film industry icon Vaughn began following Brentford over 25 years ago when a fellow actor mentioned they would be a “great club to invest in”.

He eventually decided to buy a minority stake in the West London side in 2025.



Alongside boosting Brentford’s bid “to thrive in the world’s most competitive football league, Vaughn’s investment has brought a serious touch of glamour to the Gtech Community Stadium.

He and supermodel wife Claudia Schiffer have formed a star-studded partnership in the stands on multiple occasions, with the latter once the top-paid model on the planet.

The Bees will be hoping their new Hollywood-inspired away kit can help them dazzle on and off the pitch in 2026/27.

Brentford came within a whisker of European qualification last season but were agonizingly denied by goal difference.

Sports.title: Major Arsenal transfer blow as Real Madrid plan to KEEP Vinicius Jr even if it means Brazilian leaves for free next year
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO wants to keep Vinicius Junior at Real Madrid – even if he leaves on a free next summer.

Vinicius is out of contract in June 2027 and Madrid are prepared to let him run down his deal amid intense interest from Arsenal.



Mourinho is eager to work with Vinicius, 26, even if the Brazil international is unwilling to sign a new contract at the Bernabeu.

Madrid are on the verge of completing the signing of winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig but club sources insist he is not a replacement for Vinicius.



Several former players at Madrid and Barcelona have encouraged interest from Premier League clubs before signing new contracts.

Diomande and Vinicius are both represented by the Roc Nation agency that counts Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli among its clients.

Martinelli faces an uncertain future as he has also entered the last 12 months of his contract.

Mourinho first encountered Vinicius – who could command wages of £400,000-a-week if he joined Arsenal – when he impressed on his debut for Real against Manchester United eight years ago in a friendly in Miami.

The pair had an impassioned exchange during Madrid’s 1-0 Champions League knockout win at Mourinho’s Benfica last season after Vinicius claimed he was racially abused by midfielder Gianluca Prestianni.

Mourinho spoke at length with Vinicius during the ten-minute stoppage and later said it would be “over” for Prestianni at Benfica if he was found guilty of racially abusing Vinicius.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Prestianni denied making a racist comment and was suspended for six games by Uefa after admitting he made a homophobic slur towards Vinicius.

Madrid have already bolstered their squad with the arrivals of Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate, Bernardo Silva and Denzel Dumfries, while they are also working on a move for Manchester City midfielder Rodri.

The 15-time European champions are prepared to sell midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni after a fresh enquiry from United.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta believes Vinicius would be a potential game-changing addition as the Premier League champions aim to secure a maiden Champions League.

Vinicius has won two Champions Leagues with Madrid, scoring in the 2022 and 2024 finals against Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund.



Arsenal lost last season’s final to Paris Saint-Germain in a penalty shootout.

Sports.title: PSG ‘threatening to hijack Real Madrid’s transfer for Rodri in revenge for losing out on Yan Diomande’
Sports.content:
PSG are plotting revenge on Real Madrid after losing out on winger Yan Diomande – with a hijack for Rodri on the cards, according to reports.

The French giants were one of a number of interested clubs in RB Leipzig speedster Diomande – but Jose Mourinho has come in to poach him.



A deal is yet to be fully agreed but Luis Enrique‘s men signalled their intention to back down from the transfer over the weekend.

And now they are trying to get their own back by stealing Rodri instead.



The World Cup winner is considering his options at Manchester City with just 12 months left on his current contract.

AS in Spain say that PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi is furious at Madrid coming from nowhere to get Diomande on board.

And he is described as personally giving the order for contact to be made with Rodri‘s agent and camp.

It is claimed that they are seeking to get one over Madrid by signing Rodri “at all costs.”

Qatari chief Al-Khelaifi is refusing to let European rivals Madrid overshadow them in the market after they had been finalising Diomande’s big-money arrival.

The Ivorian gave his backing to PSG over Liverpool and other suitors early on this summer but backtracked when Madrid came to the table.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And this is all regardless of what Enrique himself has to say – with the back-to-back Champions League winner already possessing a midfield of dreams.

He can pick from Vitinha, Joao Neves, Fabian Ruiz, Warren Zaire-Emery, and Lee Kang-In.

After being embarrassed by Kylian Mbappe‘s departure to the Santiago Bernabeu on a free, they are determined not to end up covered in egg again.

But City would love to keep Rodri and have offered an extension – with the player weighing up his future.



Madrid, who could yet lose Aurelien Tchouameni to Manchester United despite suggestions he has signed a new contract, have been chasing Rodri for months.

They are keen to bring him back to the Spanish capital after he left fierce local rivals Atletico in 2019.

Los Blancos have also ruled themselves publicly out of signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea – another potential midfield target.

Madrid also face a challenge to keep star attacker Vinicius Jr with Arsenal expressing interest.

Sports.title: Mo Salah’s future in limbo as European giants ‘WALK AWAY’ from transfer despite meeting with Liverpool icon three times
Sports.content:
MO SALAH has been handed a major blow after Besiktas claimed they have walked away from talks with the ex-Liverpool star.

The Egyptian is looking for his next club after leaving Anfield as a free agent at the end of the 2025/26 season.



Besiktas had emerged as a possible contender to sign the two-time Premier League winner despite links to Saudi Arabia.

But club chief Onder Ozen says the Turkish outfit have pulled out after a “deadlock” in negotiations, despite meeting Salah three times.



Ozen told the Turkish press, via the Daily Mail: “We contacted Salah, this also involved a financing model.

“Salah is a global star, a respected athlete. We met with Salah three times before the financial part of the negotiations was discussed.



“Up to this point, everything was smooth. When the financial side began, the initial smoothness slowed down from July 21 onwards.”

Ozen suggested Besiktas were unwilling to break their wage structure for Salah, who was earning around £400,000-a-week at Liverpool.

He reportedly pocketed an eye-watering £30.8million a year when performance-based bonuses were taken into account.

And Ozen said they simply couldn’t satisfy Salah’s massive demands while staying within their strict budget.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He added: “Requests began to arrive that would both disrupt the flow of information and create a deadlock in the financial process. I can assume that a respected athlete like Salah was unaware of this.

“The club has a policy, and it cannot deviate from that policy, our President has very clearly identified his position and has stayed there.

“I don’t have a chance to say yes or no, Besiktas’s offer, made under its own terms, is clear. If a response comes to this offer, it can be evaluated.

“But Besiktas will not make another offer. They said they are also in talks with another club, maybe they will get a result from there.



“The last offer we made to Salah is the final point that does not harm Besiktas’s club identity.”

Salah left Liverpool as one of the club’s greatest ever players after netting 257 goals in 442 appearances across a nine-year spell.

He won two Premier League titles, two domestic cups and the Champions League during his time at the club.

But his final season at the club ended on a sour note after giving a bombshell interview in December accusing the club of “throwing him under the bus”.

Sports.title: Football lawmakers confirm new Fifa rule was WRONGLY used at World Cup as Argentina benefitted from error
Sports.content:
IFAB has admitted that VAR wrongly intervened on two instances of diving at the World Cup.

One of them helped Argentina squeeze past Switzerland in the quarter-finals, setting up their win over England in the semis.



Swiss forward Breel Embolo thought he had won a free-kick on the edge of the box following a tackle from Leandro Paredes.

But the VAR recommended an on-field review on the basis of ‘mistaken identity’.



Referee Joao Pinheiro then watched the footage, retracted the free-kick and showed a yellow card to Embolo – his second of the night – for simulation.

Ifab, global football‘s law-making body, has now confirmed that VAR intervention on grounds of ‘mistaken identity’ can only be used if there is doubt around the identity of the culprit.



It cannot spark a review of the offence itself, meaning Embolo should have remained on the pitch and the free-kick should have stood, if the rules were applied correctly.

The score was 1-1 when Embolo was dismissed in the 72nd minute, and Argentina went on to win 3-1 in extra-time.

The Ifab update reads: “A yellow card which is not a second yellow card can only be reviewed to identify the player who committed the offence that was penalised; the offence itself cannot be reviewed/changed.

“The use of the mistaken identity clause to deal with simulation during the World Cup was well received and will be included in the detailed review of the VAR protocol announced in circular No32.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“However, it may not be used as such until that review is concluded.”

Argentina went on to lose in the final to Spain, but only after numerous instances of refereeing controversy, with beaten last-16 opponents Egypt even calling the tournament “rigged“.

The USA were the other team to benefit from a similar VAR mishap after Tim Ream was yellow carded for a tackle on Miguel Almiron in the group stage.

VAR cited ‘mistaken identity’ to recommend an on-field review, and ref Danny Makkelie reversed the decision before booking Almiron for diving.

Sports.title: UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words
Sports.content:
UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors but European football’s governing body have fired back at that plot

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino faced severe criticism throughout the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA have taken aim at FIFA and said that football is ‘not theirs to sell’ in the face of their outrageous plan. Recent reports have suggested that world football’s governing body is planning on selling stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



The scheme could see FIFA president Gianni Infantino earn millions if a deal is rubber-stamped. The administration of US President Donald Trump has reportedly been consulted.

‌



And while the plan is still being mulled over by those within the organisation, it has not gone down well within UEFA.

‌



A statement from the Champions League organisers on Tuesday afternoon read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross.

Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return READ MORE :

“UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

‌



FIFA have already explained their plan in detail. In a statement, they confirmed that FIFA intends to expand football development funding to over $10 billion (£7.49 billion). That funding would then be available to all 211 associations that are members of FIFA.

View 2 Images Trump's administration have already been told about FIFA's plan (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA would remain as majority stakeholders in the World Cup, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations would receive a small stake totalling 20 per cent.

‌



The Times has reported that one senior figure within the game has labelled FIFA’s plan as a "nuclear bomb" for the game.

FIFA President Infantino has regularly courted controversy this summer, particularly when it comes to the World Cup. Supporters took aim at him for the sky-high ticket prices during the tournament.

He was also criticised for his role in the decision to reverse Folarin Balogun’s ban for a red card. The American forward was initially suspended after being sent off, only for that decision to be reversed following a phone call from US President Trump.

Article continues below

On the criticism he faced, Infantino said : “You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all. To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness.”

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return

Italy have finally ended a week of turmoil by appointing Roberto Mancini as Claudio Ranieri is hired as technical director - replacing Paolo Maldini

View 2 Images Roberto Mancini, who won Euro 2020, is back in charge of Italy (Image: getty)

Italy's manager search has ended with Roberto Mancini taking charge for a second spell - and Claudio Ranieri coming in as the country's technical director.

‌



Monday proved a pivotal day as Azzurri legend Paolo Maldini quit after only 16 days in the job after Andrea Pirlo was blocked from taking over the four-time World Cup winners. Some senior figures at the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) shied away from his appointment due to ties to a Russian betting firm.

‌



Pirlo was the third man to be eyed for the job after Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti both said no. Mancini is the fourth man they've gone after a finally a deal has been agreed with Ranieri sitting in a senior role.

‌



The FIGC president, Giovanni Malago, said on the appointment: “Mancini is the coach. I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

Liverpool's Milos Kerkez explains why he chose to keep distance from Andy Robertson READ MORE :

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini and will oversee technical operations and elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. He's most heralded for leading Leicester to the Premier League title but has also managed Juventus, Roma and Inter Milan.

“I needed someone with whom I could share ‌the decision on the coach, because without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

‌



In hiring Mancini they bring back the last man to lead Italy to tournament glory, although either side of that they've been wholly disappointing. The former Manchester City boss replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession. He held the job from 2018 to 2023 and claimed Euro 2020 glory following a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley.

View 2 Images Italy have bought in Claudio Ranieri as technical director

Mancini ultimately presided over the Azzurri's world record 37-game unbeaten run, but couldn't qualify for the 2022 World Cup - losing to North Macedonia in a play-off - before resigning in August 2023.

‌



Italy became the first World Cup winners ever to miss out on three tournaments successively having not played at the finals since 2014, when they were knocked out in the group phase. That was also the case in 2010, marking a dire run since they claimed the World Cup in 2006.

Italy start their Nations League campaign on 25 September at home to Belgium before travelling to face Turkey three days later.

City are set to take on Inter Milan in Hong Kong before clashes with the K-League All-Stars and Atletico Madrid in South Korea. Grealish, 30, has just one year remaining on his contract with his current employers.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino plots to SELL World Cup after Donald Trump talks in ‘nuclear bomb’ for football
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino plots to SELL World Cup after Donald Trump talks in ‘nuclear bomb’ for football

Plans for selling stakes in FIFA to private investors have emerged under a highly controversial scheme, with UEFA condemning the proposals

View 2 Images Plans have emerged which could see stakes in the World Cup and FIFA reportedly made available to private investors. (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. The organisation has confirmed that they will invite third parties to make a 'minority, non-controlling investments' into the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

‌



Bank J.P. Morgan have engaged to work alongside FIFA while other advisers such as OpenEconomics are engaging with prospective long-term investors. Infantino and the FIFA administration will control the development of the project while outside investors will have a minority stake with no operational role.

‌



The administration of US President Donald Trump has reportedly been consulted about the plan, which would see a company being formed to control FIFA's men's and women's competitions, the World Cup and Club World Cup. Each of the 211 member associations would receive a stake which they could retain or sell for income.

‌



Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

The Times has reported that one senior figure within football regards the plan as a "nuclear bomb" for the game, as the proposals suggest that FIFA would own the majority of the company, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations receiving a small stake totalling 20 per cent.

UEFA have released a statement condemning the report. They said: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously.

"So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

‌



"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The venture is said to have raised concerns that private investors could put pressure on the men's World Cup being staged in countries where commercial success can be maximised. The report adds that American businessman Joshua Kushner, whose older brother Jared Kushner is married to Trump's daughter Ivanka, is seen as the main investor along with bank JP Morgan.

‌



The 56-year-old Infantino is set to be re-elected as the FIFA president until 2031 with no competitor for his position. The move to a new model could see Infantino become commissioner, with some suggesting the salary for that position could be on par with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell who earns $64million (£48m) a year, around 10 times as much as the FIFA chief's earnings.

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino alongside US President Donald Trump. (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Infantino has come in for criticism following this summer's World Cup across North America. The ticket prices, logistics surrounding the tournament and Trump's interference, which saw USA international Folarin Balogun's ban suspended, sparked intense scrutiny.

‌



A week after the tournament, the 56-year-old launched a tirade accusing critics of spreading hate. He posted a 15-slide, 887-word statement on Instagram, saying: "My message for all those who…

"To everyone who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception, and the joy. To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness.

"Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all."

Sports.title: Scandinavia retains Goodwood Cup crown after eventful race
Sports.content:
Scandinavia confirmed his superiority over Trawlerman to defend his Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup title in fine style at Goodwood.

Aidan O'Brien's son of Justify and his John and Thady Gosden-trained adversary had served up a thriller in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot and another titanic tussle looked on the cards on the Sussex Downs.

Sent off the 6-5 favourite, Ryan Moore was always hot on the heels of Trawlerman who headed affairs in the hands of William Buick, in a race that had early drama when Amiloc unshipped Hector Crouch leaving the stalls.

Amiloc would again play a key role after Buick had set sail for home heading downhill into the straight and with the two Ascot rivals knuckling down for another battle, the loose Amiloc cut across the pair, checking Trawlerman's momentum and allowing Scandinavia to scorch clear.

He galloped on eight and a half lengths into the distance as Trawlerman finished second once again to his Ballydoyle foe, with Roger Varian's Rahiebb third.

"I'm delighted, I'm thankful to everyone around him. He's a great horse, he's a real top stayer," said O'Brien.

"He's a high cruising speed, he relaxes and finds his momentum. Ryan said he finds the minute he starts asking him, he starts coming alive underneath him.

Image: Ryan Moore rode Scandinavia to Goodwood Cup success

"We were a bit worried coming to Ascot because we've never been two and a half (miles) and you're never sure until you do it.

"We felt he's really gone the right way since Ascot. It's a great race to win, very prestigious.

"It's great that Trawlerman came and all the horses were there, it's what we all want to see - win, lose or draw.

"We thought that Trawlerman was going to make it, we were hoping that he would so Ryan could just follow him as he did in Ascot.

"It was going to be very simple, was he good enough or not? Obviously there was a little bit of drama, Trawlerman was a bit slowly away and Ralph's (Beckett) horse (Amiloc) was loose.

"It was a bit eventful, but it was still a great race at a great track. It was a spectacle to watch and going two miles, you get a great chance to look at it and take it in."

Of Scandinavia's future, O'Brien added: "He's very sound, he loves what he's doing and the lads love having him.

"When you get a horse like this that can race year in, year out, that's what makes it special.

"They're very hard to find, impossible really. I would imagine he'll keep racing as long as he stays safe and sound.

"He could (emulate Yeats, four-time winner of the Gold Cup), he's a natural cruiser. He's easy to train, he's a great mind and as he's by Justify, he has that great rhythm."

Moore said: "It was nice for him to have a horse to follow all the way, he probably thinks he got beat!

"His stride never shortened, he just kept galloping all the way to the line - what more can you say?

"He likes fast ground, he's a high-class horse and hopefully there's a few more good days to come."

Kaiya Fraser shines with Vintage performance

Kaiya Fraser produced a brilliant ride to land the Coral Vintage Stakes at Goodwood aboard the unbeaten Dr Rascal and celebrated the biggest victory of his career in the process.

The winning jockey had endured the nasty experience of being pulled from the saddle of the Oliver Cole-trained colt by the bite of a loose horse before remounting to win at Ascot earlier this month.

On this occasion the 23-year-old held his nerve to squeeze through a narrow gap on the rails on the inside of David Egan on Pikachu a furlong from home, delivering the son of Sottsass to land the spoils at 13-2 by half a length from the Aidan O'Brien-trained Haffner.

Favourite Al Hudaiba once again looked a difficult ride, with William Buick struggling to get him going before finishing a close third.

Fraser said: "It means everything, this is what we wake up for every morning.

Image: Dr Rascal claimed Group 2 gold at Goodwood

"I've put so much hard work in to get where I am today and all the people around who have helped me - my agent James Forrest and all the owners and trainers who put me up.

"I'm very grateful to them and I wouldn't be here if it wasn't for them."

He added: "You saw today, he had to get a push into the stalls because he obviously had that experience last time out where he got a bit nervous, but luckily he's a willing horse and he went in with a bit of encouragement and he got out and got the job done."

This was a first victory for Cole in a race his father Paul won three times with Putra (1996), Central Park (1997) and Strategic Prince (2006).

He said: "I was always quietly confident, he's a very good horse.

"I wasn't very nervous before the race which was quite a good thing because I have a lot of faith in this horse.

"He's a very fast horse… another unlucky run really because he got loose before Ascot and then he's just got mullered coming up there in the straight and he's still won.

"We'll probably look to the Dewhurst or something like that; he's got so much class and so much speed and he's very well bred, we're very lucky to have him in our stable.

"We're not used to these kinds of horses so back to the drawing board (for plans). The Royal Lodge probably not. I'll have to go away and have a think about it.

"It means a lot (to follow in his father's footsteps). My first complete year as a trainer, it means a lot. It's not just me, there's a big group at home that work so hard - I'm very proud of all of them."

The stewards did have a look afterwards, but found Fraser and Dr Rascal had gone through a legitimate gap on the inside of Pikachu.

Fraser said: "My horse slightly came off his line and I just had to straighten him up, didn't cause anything.

"I'm delighted, first Group winner - in a Group Two on a very nice two-year-old, so I'm looking forward to the future."

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr to stay at Real Madrid beyond this summer
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior will be staying at Real Madrid beyond this summer, Sky Sports News has been told.

The Spanish club have no intention of selling him and are confident he will agree a new contract.

This is despite the interest of Arsenal, who are monitoring his situation closely with a year remaining on his current deal.

On Monday, Sky Sports News broke the news that further talks over his future between Real and his representatives will take place this week. That is with the intention of making progress on a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu.

New manager Jose Mourinho is understood to value Vinicius highly and wants him to remain one of his top Galacticos.

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas:

The situation regarding Vinicius Junior has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest and further talks to come.

But there is no strong public evidence yet that Vinicius wants to leave Real Madrid for any reason, sporting or otherwise; no quotes, no interviews, no suggestive social media posts.

Real Madrid and - most importantly - new manager Jose Mourinho want him to stay and agree new terms.

Club president Florentino Perez is personally involved and has publicly expressed a desire for Vinicius to stay long term. Reports in Spain have long claimed that both parties have indicated a preference for him to remain at the club. Real Madrid do not want him to run down the deal into a free agent situation either.

Vinicius is more than just an outstanding left winger. He is a global superstar - and a Galactico in every sense. In that way he embodies everything about Real Madrid and fits right in.

Can the same be said about Arsenal? Signing such an icon has not been part of Mikel Arteta's Arsenal project so far, however exciting it might be to go in that direction.

Sports.title: Why has Hamilton received so many penalties and what have they cost him?
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has received four penalties from the stewards in the last three Formula 1 race weekends - an unusually high number for any driver over such a short period.

After his latest penalty in Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix for speeding in the pit lane, Hamilton stated on the radio that the stewards are "handing out penalties like crazy".

The result was that Hamilton lost further crucial points in the title race, and he now trails Kimi Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, so have the penalties been justified?

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

British Grand Prix - false start

Finishing Position: Third

Points lost: Likely none

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New angles of Lewis Hamilton's false start at British GP

Hamilton was handed a five-second time penalty for jumping the start at the British Grand Prix when he was deemed to be creeping forward before the lights went out.

He went on to finish third, perhaps fortunately after knocking down his pit mechanic at a late pit stop, so the penalty likely did not impact his result. Hamilton considered the penalty harsh.

"We talked in the drivers' briefing the fact that they're inconsistent with this stuff. Drivers in the past have moved and not been penalised," he said.

"We discussed that, as long as you're not moving when the last lights are on, you shouldn't be penalised. I wasn't out of my box. And they agreed. So they're looking into that for the future."

Belgian Grand Prix - causing a collision

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to six

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

Hamilton was given a five-second time penalty for being "wholly at fault" for colliding with George Russell on the opening lap of the British Grand Prix at Turn 5.

On the inside line, Hamilton understeered into Russell and was "unable to maintain sufficient separation" which led to the contact and Russell spinning into the gravel and out of the race.

But, Russell himself said the contact was a "racing incident" even though he came off worse.

Hamilton said: "Even the driver I collided with said that it was just a racing incident. I think that one was not needed. But that cost me a lot of points."

Hamilton benefited from pitting and serving his penalty under a Virtual Safety Car, but without the penalty he would almost certainly have been on the podium rather than finishing fourth.

He may even have had a fighting chance of victory given his team-mate Charles Leclerc was only overtaken by race-winner Antonelli with 10 laps to go. A battle with Leclerc was definitely on the cards for second.

Hungarian Grand Prix Qualifying - impeding

Starting Position: Fifth

Impact: Potential to lead race and fight for win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's was given a grid penalty for blocking Oscar Piastri in qualifying in Hungary

Hamilton was hit with a three-grid place penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri during the final part of Qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

After completing his final Q3 run, where he did not improve, Hamilton was not told Piastri was starting his flying lap, so effectively blocked the McLaren driver through Turn 1.

"That was really just unfortunate. I take responsibility for ultimately being on track. I should have looked in my mirrors," said Hamilton.

"But I thought everyone would have been at the end of the first lap. The information I got was right at the end. A communication error."

Hamilton was not happy that Ferrari sent himself and Leclerc out first for the last Q3 runs, which partly led to the impeding incident with Piastri.

He had qualified second and, with brand-new soft tyres, would have had a golden chance to take the lead on the first lap and potentially win the race. Instead, he started fifth and was penalised again in the Grand Prix.

Hungarian Grand Prix - speeding in the pit lane

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to three

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson analyses Lewis Hamilton's speeding in the pit lane that handed him a five-second time penalty

The final race before the summer break was not well executed by Ferrari and Hamilton, who endured a difficult time after being overtaken by Max Verstappen after the first round of pit stops.

But Hamilton was still potentially on course for second until a Virtual Safety Car with 13 laps to go led Ferrari to pit for new fresh tyres.

In the pit lane, Hamilton exceeded the 80kph speed limit by 0.1kph as he was eager to beat Antonelli on the merge between pit exit and track.

It was a driver mistake but Hamilton thought, with hindsight, he should not have pitted and would have been third without the stop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

"The call came literally just before the pit lane entry and I didn't have time to debate and you've got to trust the decision that has been taken," he told Sky Sports F1.

"In hindsight, my tyres were totally fine. I was probably going to lose out to Max but I think I could have kept third at least. Then just opened up the door to obviously the penalty that I got in the end."

Hamilton: I can't give stewards any reason to penalise me

Apart from the Belgium collision with Russell, all of Hamilton's penalties are hard, or impossible, to argue against. He has probably only lost six points from the in-race penalties but the impeding in Qualifying at the Hungaroring was the most detrimental.

Ferrari had great pace in Budapest and track position is king, so a good start on softs from the front row of the grid likely would have seen Hamilton in the lead.

His raw speed has been very strong recently, too, so victory was possible on Sunday and he would have been less than 40 points behind Antonelli.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton responds to his speeding penalty from Budapest

Ferrari and Hamilton must cut out these unforced errors if they want that record-breaking eighth world drivers' title.

"I'll work hard to try and come back. There's still a lot of positives to take. I'm going to try and make sure I don't give them any reason to penalise me," said Hamilton.

Sports.title: Joao Pedro nets hat-trick as Chelsea score SIX in Alonso's first game
Sports.content:
Joao Pedro scored a nine-minute hat-trick as Xabi Alonso began his Chelsea reign with a ridiculous 6-4 victory over Western Sydney Wanderers in pre-season.

Chelsea led through 17-year-old Dastan Satpaev in only the sixth minute, yet managed to fall behind three times to the A-League side before substitute Joao Pedro showed his class with a late treble in Sydney.

Alonso named a youthful side in a 4-2-3-1 formation with Tosin and Liam Delap the only significant senior experience in the starting XI before introducing the likes of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, Estevao and Levi Colwill midway through the second half.

How Chelsea lined up First half (4-2-3-1): Sharman-Lowe; Acheampong, Subuloye, Tosin, Emenalo; Watson, Essugo; Kavuma-McQueen, Walsh, Satpaev; Delap.

From the 64th minute: Sanchez; Palestra, Colwill, Fofana, Anselmino; Watson, Nicoll-Jazuli; Estevao, Palmer, Gittens; Joao Pedro.

Chelsea's first two goals, the second coming from Dario Essugo, were brilliant moves from back to front on a bumpy pitch used primarily for rugby league matches, and were a sign of the style Alonso will hope to implement at Stamford Bridge.

But their defending was poor and after being level at the break, Alonso's side were trailing in the 64th minute by the time he brought on his stars, deploying Palmer in the No 10 role with Estevao on the right and Jamie Gittens on the other side.

Gittens levelled two minutes after his introduction for 3-3, yet Estevao's slack pass left youngster Reggie Watson short deep inside their own half, and Western Sydney substitute Awan Lual punished the error to restore their lead with little over 10 minutes remaining.

But then the Joao Pedro show started. He finished expertly from inside the box to bring Chelsea level again, slotted home to give them the lead after being played in by Palmer and then tapped in his third from a couple of yards at a corner to seal a remarkable hat-trick and the win.

What did we learn from Alonso's debut?

Sky Sports' Ron Walker:

There's always a word of caution about reading too much into the opening game of pre-season, especially with so many first-team players missing for Chelsea.

But there are certainly a few takeaways from Xabi Alonso's debut in the dugout...

Flexible formation - Chelsea defended in a four but with the ball, Landon Emenalo bombed forward down the left and often overlapped Dastan Satpaev down that flank. It did leave Chelsea open at the back, though.

You can't argue with a nine-minute hat-trick Defensive concerns - Josh Acheampong and Tosin were two of Chelsea's more senior players to start the game in Sydney but both found life difficult against a side who finished bottom of the A-League last season. They were offered little cover by the visitors' midfield at times.

Alonso: We need to manage games better

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso said:

"It has been a very useful friendly that we can learn a lot from today. There were moments when we were struggling to find solutions, and we needed this. The positive is that we corrected them, but there were moments when the game management is something that we can learn from today.

"When they were pressing so high, it was tough to find the solution from inside, to have a different understanding of what's happening, and to make those changes in the game.

"It's something that will happen often in all the games, and the more situations we struggle with and find solutions, the better team we will be. For that, I think that this friendly is going to be useful for the future, and as well for minutes for everyone."

Sports.title: The science behind Luke Littler's trophy-laden success
Sports.content:
Want to know the secret behind the success of darting phenom Luke Littler?

Littler has spearheaded darts' surge towards the mainstream since he broke on the scene with his debut run to the 2024 World Championship final as a 16-year-old.

Darts manufacturer Target Darts has supported the global superstar since the age of 12. In February 2024, the teenager signed a multi-year mega-deal reported to be worth up to £20 million - the most lucrative the sport has ever seen.

The science behind Littler's darts

Luke Littler uses 23g Target Luke Littler Gen 1 (G1) 90% tungsten darts featuring a straight barrel design.



Barrel and Grip Specifications



Material: 90% tungsten alloy with a black PVD coating.



Weight: 23 grams.Dimensions: 52 mm length and 6.5 mm width.



Grip Design: Dual pixel grip and deep ring cuts at the front/centre, with finer radial grooves at the rear.



Shafts and Flights Setup



Points: Extended custom points (around 40mm to 45mm Swiss/nano points) for tighter grouping.



Shafts & Flights: Target K-Flex integrated flight and intermediate shaft system, typically using No.6 shape flights.



Littler possesses a generational talent when it comes to playing darts and Sky Sports pundit Wayne Mardle has said "he's probably the most natural naturally gifted player I've ever seen in my life".

Since the moment the Warrington-born star first held a dart, he's become a record-breaker and history-maker.

James Tattersall, CEO of Target Darts, says both the company and Littler are "aligned" in where they want to see the future of darts go.

Speaking at an event in which Target have set out a vision to inspire 100 million people to play darts by the end of the decade, he explained the process of how Littler sat down with chairman Garry Plummer, the design team, and engineers to build darts to perfect his game.

"I think some of the inspiration was drawn from Adrian Lewis' darts and the pixel grip, which is a unique grip that Target has and that worked its way into building up Luke's original G1," said Tattersall. "That was the barrel, but over the years Luke's tweaked it and challenged us to improve it. The point length has changed, the shaft and flight have changed to a K-Flex system before his first World Championships."

F-Flex is a one-piece flight and shaft innovation that screws into the back of the barrel.

Tattersall explained: "What it helps you do is when you're throwing darts together in such tight groupings like Luke does, the thing you want to avoid is that dart coming in and deflecting off the dart that's already in the board and the K-Flex helps reduce those deflections substantially.

"And longer points - it's like the balance of the dart and how it flies and how it lands through the air. I think another part of it is it keeps the barrel section of the dart further away from the treble and that creates more space in the board."

Talent vs Equipment?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Matchplay final between Luke Littler and Gerwyn Price

"His talent is all down to him," says Tattersall. "I think when you're talking about the equipment, we're talking about making Luke comfortable with all of that talent and giving him the right equipment that he's confident with to use and just to get those last few percentages, but Luke's an extraordinary player regardless."

With two world titles in three visits to Alexandra Palace, and 14 major titles to his name, Littler is well on his way to joining Phil Taylor as a legend of the sport.

The problem for his rivals is that he is still getting better after the Warrington star crushed Gerwyn Price 18-9 to retain his Betfred World Matchplay title in Blackpool on Sunday.

Littler was in imperious form as he set a new record for the final with an average of 111.53, lifting his average for the tournament as a whole to 111.04 to break Phil Taylor's previous high mark of 106.31.

The win keeps Littler on course for a clean sweep of trophies in 2026 having already won the World Championship, UK Open, Premier League and the Masters.

The supporting cast behind Littler

Image: Littler is benefitting from a huge supporting cast

Littler's management have invested in sports psychologists, nutritionists, performance coaches, and biomechanics in order to get the most out of their talent, and the teenager has benefitted in every area to help support his game.

"Mentality is absolutely key. We want to protect the players. The stage is lonely up there, and darts is a gruelling sport," Tattersall said.

"It's a bit like a penalty shootout, but every single time you're throwing a dart. It's such a closed skill, and it's so repetitive. Your mindset's got to be really, really clear, and you get those big momentum swings, you think you're about to checkout the double, you miss by a millimetre, your opponent throws in a big 170 checkout, and that's a punch in the stomach. It's how do you recover from that for the next leg? That's sports psychology, and it's crucial in all sports. I don't know why it's a surprise that it should not be in darts."

'We want to learn about action - not create robots'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler smashed in six brilliant 100+ checkouts as he reclaimed the World Matchplay title in Blackpool

With biomechanics, the cameras observe how a player throws darts, with sports science data helping ways of working on the technique in order to improve.

Target have ideas but Tattersall insists implementing them will not turn the Luke Littlers of this world into robots.

"That's the last thing we want to do," he said. "What we want to do is discover and learn about the sport, and learn about that action, because why is it that there are different throwing techniques?

"If you look at something like golf, where you know suddenly you come along with the Vardon grip [or overlapping grip], and that becomes almost the only way to hold a golf club.

"I think the high jump has got that really famous example of how the sport, science, innovated, [Fosbury flop], you ended up with that kind of one technique point.

"I think there will always be different ways of throwing a dart, and there will be different ways of improving those different styles, and maybe that particular style is because you're tall, and maybe that particular style is because you've got longer arms, we don't know yet, but that's what we're going to find out, and then use that data accordingly."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler discusses the levels he's reaching at the moment and how it compares to the legendary Phil Taylor

Zoe Burton, Chief Transformation Officer at Target Darts, says Littler is already inspiring the next generation with his natural talent, although the company are slowly moving towards a performance technology system, which is currently being tested on a number of players.

"If you look at a young person and you think of their journey as they get into a sport, you need an inspiring player - that person who they look up to - and can almost aspire to be. Luke Littler provides that," said Buton.

"You need a natural talent, but that gets you so far. Then it's determination and I think psychology as well.

"What makes a star player become a great and world-class player is actually their ability to focus under pressure and make those doubles It's never going to be robotic."

Who will win this year's BoyleSports World Grand Prix? World No 1 Luke Littler will be defending his title and you can watch all the action on Sky Sports. Stream darts and more top sport with NOW.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso plays down Welbeck and Henderson moves after Chelsea win
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso refused to confirm Chelsea are interested in signing the veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson after his first game in charge of the team, a 6-4 pre-season victory against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday, but said he was looking to build a squad that had “proper balance”.

Chelsea are understood to be in talks over a surprise move to sign the 35-year-old Welbeck from Brighton, with the club also reportedly interested in signing the 36-year-old Henderson from Brentford. The links to two Premier League stalwarts reflects a revised transfer strategy under Alonso, with Chelsea seeking to recruit more experienced players into their squad as opposed to be solely focused on signing young players, often tying them to lengthy contracts.

“I’m sure that from today to the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of links, a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them, it’s going to be a hard task,” Alonso said. “But for sure, we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance. We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team.”

The new Chelsea manager fielded a youthful side at the Accor Stadium at Sydney Olympic Park in Homebush, with Liam Delap and Tosin Adarabioyo the most experienced members of the starting lineup. Alonso waited until the 63rd minute to bring on a host of star names, including Cole Palmer and João Pedro. The Brazilian forward, who missed out on a place in Carlo Ancelotti’s World Cup squad, made a significant impact off the bench, scoring a hat-trick in just nine minutes as Chelsea took control of the game against their A-League opponents.

João Pedro scored 20 goals during an excellent debut season for Chelsea, having arrived from Brighton for £60m 12 months ago, and asked about the player’s mood before the upcoming campaign, Alonso said: “Very hungry. João is really, really determined to have a great season. He wants to, after a great last year, when he scored many goals. He wants to keep scoring more and more.”

A number of Chelsea’s youngsters showed plenty of promise, with the 17-year-old Dastan Satpayev opening the scoring after six minutes. The Kazakh forward is yet to sign officially for the club and is playing in pre-season as a triallist. His opening goal came from a defence-splitting pass from another teenager, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, with Satpayev smashing the ball home at the near post.

Chelsea’s back four struggled in the first half against a lively Wanderers frontline and their reported new set-piece coach, Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee, will have plenty to work on judging by the ease with which Brandon Borrello and Anthony Pantazopoulos won headers from a corner as the latter scored at the back post for the hosts.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming on as a second-half substitute. Photograph: Mark Evans/EPA

The Wanderers took the lead through Aydan Hammond before a lovely finish from the Portuguese midfielder Dário Essugo made it 2-2 at the break. The goals kept coming in the second half when the left-back Landon Emenalo, who impressed in attack, saw his clearance deflected into the path of Dylan Scicluna who put the Sydney side 3-2 ahead. Alonso then turned to his bench and his substitutions made an immediate impact. João Pedro held off a number of challenges on the edge of the box before pulling the ball back to Jamie Gittens who fired home from close range.
