But this topsy-turvy game, which felt like England’s third-place playoff against France at the World Cup and finished with the same scoreline, provided more entertainment as the Australian side went ahead for a third time after Estêvão Willian lost possession on the edge of his own area. Awan Lual was on hand to slide the ball through Robert Sánchez’s legs to put his side 4-3 ahead.

The Wanderers, who are also in pre-season, again failed to hold on to a lead as Chelsea overpowered a team that finished bottom of their domestic league last season. João Pedro looked sharp as he showed great composure to score twice in five minutes, before scrambling home an effort from a corner to wrap up his match-winning exploits.

João Pedro’s performance was in stark contrast to Delap, who has been repeatedly linked with a move away from west London. The 23-year-old endured another frustrating evening for Chelsea, going close on two occasions but failing to find the back of the net. Assessing Delap’s attitude since returning from the summer break, Alonso said: “I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football, feeling good and he’s doing great.”

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy head coach with Claudio Ranieri named technical director
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini has agreed to be Italy head coach for a second time, the president of the Italian Football ​Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malagò said on Tuesday, also confirming Claudio Ranieri would take over as technical director.

Mancini replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession, and returns to a job he held between 2018 and 2023. He led the national team to European Championship glory in 2021 with a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley but then failed to reach the 2022 World Cup and a slow start to Euro 2024 qualifying. In total, Mancini managed Italy for 58 matches during his first spell and at club level has managed Inter, Fiorentina and Manchester City, where he spent three years and guided them to their first Premier League title in 2011-12.

“Mancini is the coach,” Malago ‌said on Tuesday. “I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

The former FIGC technical director ‌Paolo Maldini and his adviser, Leonardo, resigned from their roles on Monday after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as head coach was blocked because of the former midfielder’s ties to a Russian betting firm. Pep Guardiola was the association’s first choice but turned down the job last month.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini. The 74-year-old, who led Leicester City to the Premier League title in ​2016, will oversee technical operations and ​elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. “I needed someone with ​whom I could share ‌the decision on ​the coach, because ​without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s back’: Zinedine Zidane named France head coach in long-awaited homecoming
Sports.content:
For Tuesday’s front page, L’Équipe simply went with “Il revient” – “He’s back” – echoing their 2005 headline when Zinédine Zidane came out of international retirement. At the time, the midfielder’s upcoming return was seen as a major boost to Les Bleus’ ailing World Cup qualifying campaign. There was a similar sense of anticipation now as the roads around the French football federation (FFF) headquarters in Paris were closed off for Zidane’s unveiling as head coach. A crowd of France fans had gathered outside by the overground metro tracks with flags, flares, and drums, as more than a hundred journalists and TV cameras were ushered into the building.

The fact Zidane would be next in line to lead France after Didier Deschamps had been an open secret for several years, and by the end of the World Cup his arrival was all but confirmed. The new head coach would enter the press conference room on Tuesday morning only minutes after his appointment was confirmed by the FFF’s executive committee, but the feeling in France was that the occasion was a couple of decades in the making.

“It’s a new cycle,” the FFF president, Philippe Diallo, proclaimed after a preamble in which he paid tribute to Deschamps’ 14-year tenure. Talks with the 1998 World Cup hero, Diallo said, began in February 2025, the month after Deschamps announced he would step down this summer. “Zinédine Zidane is one of the legends of French football, and he had made it known that it was one of his dreams to manage the French national team,” Diallo then explained. “We wanted someone with the aura, the ability, and the hearts of our fans and the French people to manage what is one of the best national teams in the world.”

View image in fullscreen France supporters gather in Paris to celebrate the confirmation of one of the greatest players in Les Blues’ history as their new head coach. Photograph: Teresa Suárez/EPA

For Zidane, this announcement was the culmination of nearly half a decade of waiting in the wings. “I had several offers from clubs in the last four to five years, but I turned them all down for France,” the former midfielder and Real Madrid insisted. “The national team is the only thing I wanted. I’ve been with the French teams since I was a kid, all the way up to the senior team. I’m a bit emotional. You might not be able to tell, but I am incredibly excited.” Zidane went as far as declaring that it was the greatest day of his managerial career. “It’s an immense joy,” he said. “I am ready for the challenge.”

The five years that have passed since the end of Zidane’s second spell in Madrid will have been spent preparing to take over Les Bleus. “I’ve been watching France as a supporter, but also as a future manager,” he explained. “I don’t think there are any traps. It’s new to me, but I’m not scared. This is what I wanted.”

The 54-year-old’s first public appearance as head coach was light on the details of his plans for the national team. He notably sidestepped a question about whether Kylian Mbappé would remain captain, insisting that he would have to meet the team and its “extraordinary players” first of all. “We need to keep this team winning,” he said, adding that he was impressed with what he had seen during the World Cup.

“I was a No 10 in my playing days,” the new head coach responded when asked about the style of play he would look to implement. Whether his answer implies a continuation of Deschamps’ attacking shift remains to be seen, but his answers did hint at some kind of change of direction. “Laurent [Blanc] was Laurent, Didier was Didier, and Zizou is Zizou,” he playfully added.

One of Zidane’s long-term objectives will be to compete with the reigning world champions, who have now beaten France in three consecutive tournament semi-finals, including in the 2025 Nations League. “I spent 25 years in Spain, and you know what that means,” he acknowledged, before pointing out that the task ahead went beyond beating La Roja. “I know Spanish football very well, but they won’t be the only opponents. You have to beat all of the teams.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was sent off by Horazio Elizondo for butting Italy’s Marco Materazzi in the chest in the 2006 World Cup final. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Zidane’s four-year contract will begin next month, with his extended staff to be unveiled a few weeks before the first international break of the new season, which starts on 21 September and includes four Nations League group matches. “We’ll see each other again in September to talk about it,” he went on. “It’s a good thing that we’ll have three weeks with the players.” The focus for now, Zidane insisted, is on his first match, which will be away to Turkey.

His homecoming, meanwhile, will be against Italy, just over 20 years after his dramatic exit from the international stage, with a red card against the same opposition in the 2006 World Cup final. If the raucous reception as he stepped out of the FFF headquarters is anything to go by, it will be one of the more memorable evenings in the Stade de France’s history.

Sports.title: Milos Kerkez: ‘I’m delighted – Andoni Iraola is the perfect fit for Liverpool’
Sports.content:
It has been quite the summer for Milos Kerkez. There was time at home in Serbia, holidays in Montenegro and Spain, a frantic knock on his bedroom door one day to tell him that Arne Slot had been sacked, an unexpected reunion with Andoni Iraola shortly afterwards, and thousands of well‑wishes sent his way after being photographed escorting a bride into church in his hometown of Vrbas. Congratulations on the wedding are also extended at the start of our interview on a rooftop terrace at Liverpool’s team hotel.

“No! This is wrong, everyone gets this wrong!” the full-back exclaims. “It was my oldest brother. In Serbia it is normal for the younger brothers to take the bride to the church. That’s what I did and now everyone thinks I got married. It was Rade, not me. There are three of us – Rade is the oldest, I’m the youngest and Marko is the middle one. I keep having to explain to people that I never got married. I was going around the club when we started back and people were congratulating me. I’m like: ‘No, I’m not ready for this yet!’”

Well, that’s one way of breaking the ice with an interviewee. Marriage is categorically not on the agenda for Kerkez, a humorous and engaging force of energy, but he is ready to embrace other responsibilities: notably stepping out of Andy Robertson’s shadow and stepping up at Liverpool. Early days, of course, but it has been noted during Liverpool’s pre‑season training camp at Chicago Fire’s performance centre how the 22-year-old and his fellow Hungary international Dominik Szoboszlai have taken a leading role among a relatively young squad.

Kerkez – who was eligible to play for Hungary through his paternal grandparents – is in an advantageous position as the Iraola era begins with gruelling double training sessions and a pre-season friendly win over Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. He knows the new boss better than any other Liverpool player, having matured into a £40m left-back during two seasons with Iraola at Bournemouth. He knows he doesn’t have to win over the new head coach as Iraola rates him highly. And he knows that, to convince Liverpool fans after a difficult debut season at Anfield, he is now working for a coach who can bring the best out of him.

View image in fullscreen Milos Kerkez tussles with Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga during a difficult debut season at Anfield. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

“I was delighted, honestly,” Kerkez says on discovering Liverpool’s choice to replace Slot. “He helped me and improved me a lot in the two years I spent with him. I was really happy, obviously for myself but also for the team. Everyone knows what type of football he plays so I think he is the perfect fit for us.

“It’s the intensity. He’s not scared to play one-on-one all over the pitch, to press high and to be on the front foot always. If you see footage of how we all are after training, all lying down, then you can see what he is preparing us for. You definitely need legs and good condition for what he wants us to do, but we will be all right. When we play games with three or four teams he calls it ‘consequences’ and the losing team and the team that finishes second has to run. How much you have to run depends on what he decides in that moment, but there is always running for the team that loses.

“He’s intense and he likes details. He’s very professional. He likes to talk sometimes but not a lot. I think maybe he doesn’t want to get too close to some players and wants to show that everyone is the same in the team, so he doesn’t want to get too close to anyone in particular. He keeps it professional, with a lot of hard work.”

There were times last season when Kerkez appeared inhibited by Slot’s insistence on building from the back and full-backs coming inside. It was his pace and energy up and down the flank with Bournemouth that had attracted Liverpool and earned him a place in the Professional Footballers’ Association’s team of the year in 2024-25. He should be able to play to his strengths more often next season.

As he explains: “The gaffer likes to play more with the full-backs down the line, underlapping, overlapping. It worked well for me at Bournemouth, so I think it will also work well for me here. He always told me that defending is really important, for him that is first of all, and because you are a full-back you need to defend really hard. Everything you can do in front of you is like a bonus. So I was always focused first on defending and then running forward to help the wingers. He showed me that when you do your job then you are free to do what you want, so I felt really free with him. He lets you be more free to do your stuff.”

Not that Kerkez blames Slot for last season’s turbulence, far from it. The pair remain in contact. “I was surprised,” he says of the Dutchman’s sacking, 12 months after delivering the Premier League title. “I really didn’t know. I was back in Serbia, I was sleeping and my brother woke me up. He knocks on my door and it was a big surprise. Nobody knew. I couldn’t believe it, I was like: ‘Wow.’ I have been in touch with him since, we have exchanged a few messages.”

View image in fullscreen Milos Kerkez celebrates scoring at a time he was playing brilliantly well for Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Kerkez admits last season was “tough for everyone” at Liverpool as every time the team seemed to have solved one problem, another would appear. As part of the expensive recruitment drive of last summer that failed to bear fruit – though Kerkez achieved far more than others – the scrutiny on the left-back and his fellow new signings was particularly intense. He insists he did not feel it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Honestly, I don’t care about pressure,” says the full-back, who will face Wrexham in the second game of Liverpool’s US tour in New York on Wednesday. “I don’t like ‘pressure’ and that stuff. I grew up a bit different in Serbia. We grew up different. You could say maybe we are built a bit different. For example, I started to drive a truck when I was 10 years old.” Sorry? “It was with my dad,” Kerkez says. “I climbed in and then I took the wheel. He was doing the pedals, I was only quite small so I couldn’t reach them.”

Kerkez’s father, Sebastijan, still drives his son to Liverpool’s training centre on occasions. He and Kerkez’s mother, Tijana, moved to England to help their second son settle into life as a Premier League player. “They are very important,” says the defender. “My brothers have their own lives now but my parents are with me and I am much happier they are with me. My dad is here to smack me sometimes on the top of the head and to remind me. Sometimes you play a few good games and maybe you start to get a bit carried away. But my dad is here to smack me. I come straight back down and I switch straight back on.”

Another important influence on Kerkez has been Robertson, the man – and the Liverpool legend – he was bought to replace. The Scotland captain and now Tottenham left-back regularly took Kerkez aside last season to pass on his experience. But there was no big parting message when the time came for Robertson to say goodbye to Anfield in May.

“I didn’t want to get a lot on to him,” says Kerkez, who became close friends with Mohamed Salah last season. “He was a bit emotional as everything was coming to an end. I didn’t want to get on to him too much, but throughout the year he helped me. We had a few conversations about crosses and about the big lungs we need to have so we can run until tomorrow. He did a lot of seasons, I should also have the same. We had conversations like that. Also, where to put the last ball, to focus, to put your head up and sometimes put better crosses in.

“We all know what Andy did for the club. I’m not running away from that. I want to make my own way. I’m going to work hard. I know what it means to play for Liverpool. I showed it a bit last year and I am going to show it more this year. Before we left the Axa [Liverpool’s training ground, to come to Chicago] I saw on TV a show about how many goals and assists Mo had, it was something like 380. I just walked out! ‘What is this?’ I was thinking. Time flies. A new generation comes and hopefully everything will be good.”

Sports.title: Sunderland close in on Dayann Methalie signing after Newcastle back off
Sports.content:
Sunderland are poised to sign the long-time Newcastle target Dayann Methalie from Toulouse. The France Under-21s defender, who can play left-back or wingback and also operate in the centre, has attracted widespread interest this summer but Régis Le Bris now appears close to acquiring him for about £26m.

Newcastle had extensively scouted Methalie, who made 27 Ligue 1 appearances for Toulouse last season, and reportedly tried to sign him in January. The club have now indicated they opted against the idea of recruiting the 20-year-old and have not submitted a bid this summer. Nonetheless, Methalie appeared an ideal fit for Newcastle’s new transfer policy of recruiting young players in the £20m-£40m price bracket.

Sunderland can offer the 6ft 2in defender Europa League football and he is understood to have verbally agreed a five-year deal at the Stadium of Light, where he would not merely be coached by a compatriot in Le Bris but be part of a sizeable contingent of French-speaking players including Enzo Le Fée, Nordi Mukiele and Habib Diarra. Methalie will be Le Bris’s second summer signing after the arrival of the Belgium right-back Thomas Meunier, who arrived on a free transfer after leaving Lille.

While Methalie is likely to face considerable competition from Reinildo to establish himself as Sunderland’s first-choice left-back, his amalgam of impressive recovery pace, robust physicality and assured left foot have seen him shine as a left-sided central defender in a back three and a back four.

Newcastle, meanwhile, remain in the market for cover at left-back and right-back, with the latter position one Eddie Howe is particularly anxious to reinforce after Kieran Trippier’s departure at the end of last season.

Howe’s hopes of keeping Bruno Guimarães appear to still rest on Arsenal’s willingness or otherwise to pay a fee in the region of £80m for the 28-year-old captain, who has been on a post-World Cup holiday in Brazil and is due to return to Newcastle on Friday, before travelling to a training camp at La Manga with the rest of the first-team squad.

Joe Willock’s future at St James’ Park also remains uncertain. Although Newcastle have rejected an offer in the region of £10m from Besiktas for the former Arsenal midfielder, they appear open to selling him, albeit for a fee closer to £20m.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester United to sign Juve’s Francisco Conceição?
Sports.content:
As sports fans everywhere eagerly await the resumption of cricket’s County Championship season, what better way to while away a few minutes than to contemplate the latest football transfer rumours?

Manchester United and Michael Carrick want to sign the 23-year-old Portugal winger Francisco Conceição from Juventus. The tricky former Porto player, who recently returned from the World Cup, is valued at about £43m (€50m). United are also said to be ahead of Chelsea in the race to snap up Alex Scott from Bournemouth.

Real Madrid, meanwhile, have increased their offer to RB Leipzig for Yan Diomande – whom Leipzig had hoped to replace with Conceição – to about £98m. Reports in Germany say further talks are in order to get the deal for the 19-year-old Côte d’Ivoire international over the line.

Liverpool have emerged as favourites to sign the France international Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, having reportedly held preliminary talks with the 23-year-old over a lucrative transfer.

Bruno Guimarães continues to be the subject of strong interest from the Premier League champions, Arsenal. Newcastle, naturally, have insisted the Brazilian is not for sale, but personal terms have reportedly been agreed between the Gunners and Guimarães’s people, so a bid is surely imminent. Arsenal are also being linked with Vinícius Júnior, with Mikel Arteta apparently determined to sign the Madrid and Brazil forward. Speculation reached fever pitch on Tuesday when it was reported Vinícius would not train this week, further increasing uncertainty over his future. José Mourinho is keen to keep the winger.

Paris Saint-Germain have distanced themselves from a move the for all-conquering Manchester City midfielder Rodri, but the Premier League club expect an offer from Real Madrid.

Seemingly having fought off Chelsea’s pursuit of Granit Xhaka, Sunderland are ready to boost their defensive options by signing the full-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.

Over in Spain, it has been reported that Sevilla are ready to sell Ruben Vargas for about £17m and Aston Villa, Newcastle and Brighton are among potential suitors in His Majesty’s Premier League.

Leeds are poised to confirm a £40m deal for James Trafford, who re-signed for Manchester City after a couple of seasons at Burnley, while Manchester United are keen to send Joshua Zirkzee on a season-long loan to Juventus, with an option for the Bianconeri to buy the 25-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea have held talks with the Brighton forward Danny Welbeck (35) and are also keen to sign Jordan Henderson (36). Welbeck knocked in 13 Premier League goals for the Seagulls last season and was fancied as a possible option for England at the World Cup, while Henderson made the cut, only to suffer a freak wrist injury. Chelsea are presumably drawing up eight-year contracts for both veterans.

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund have agreed to sign the midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas from Racing Genk in Belgium, for a fee that could rise to £32m.

And John Stones, a free agent after leaving Manchester City, has moved closer to completing his move to Inter as reported in these pages: a deal has been verbally agreed.

Sports.title: Mind the ever-growing gap: the Premier League keeps spending big
Sports.content:
The financial power of the Premier League is unmatched. The teams in England’s top division have collectively invested more than £1.4bn in new players already this summer (through disclosed fees alone), around £303m more than the 76 clubs from the Bundesliga, La Liga, Ligue 1 and Serie A combined.

These figures are the gross spend, so take no account of players sold to help balance the books. Factoring this in only increases the divide. The clubs of Ligue 1 and the Bundesliga are £203.4m and £72.2m in credit from their transfer dealings respectively. While La Liga (£163.1m) and Serie A (£124.1m) have spent more than they have earned, they are an ocean adrift of the Premier League’s net spend of £523.6m.

None of this is new; it has been the trend for many years. The worrying aspect for teams across the continent is that the gap between the Premier League and the rest may grow wider before the summer is out.

Despite their enormous outlay, top-flight English teams have spent about £230m less than Premier League clubs of 2025-26 had at this point last year. But only 25 deals were completed by the end of 1 July (which is when new contracts usually start, explaining why pre-arranged moves are often finalised then). It’s roughly half as many as the 47 that occurred by that date last summer. The expanded World Cup will probably have delayed some deals, creating a potential backlog of transfer spending that will soon hit the books.

Assessing clubs individually highlights why most might continue spending. Aston Villa, Brighton and Tottenham have already spent more in gross terms than in the entirety of the summer 2025 transfer window. Unai Emery has a net £109.6m burning a hole in his pocket following business which includes the departures of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans. Brighton will need a larger squad as they have a Conference League campaign on the horizon while Tottenham are hoping to improve upon consecutive 17th-place finishes. Their trading may not be complete even though they’ve already outspent their efforts from last summer, with Spurs’ net spend of £149.7m the highest in Europe’s big five leagues.

Chelsea also have a higher net spend than last year, even before their reportedly agreed deal for Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix goes through. Even if that transfer is not completed, would you bet against BlueCo throwing more money around, especially with a new manager to back? Danny Welbeck is the latest to emerge on the Stamford Bridge radar. Either way, Chelsea have already invested more in new talent than they had on this day last year. The same is true for Everton, Fulham, Manchester City and Newcastle, all of whom may have further incomings in the pipeline, too.

There are other clubs with work to do. The three promoted teams have only spent £8m more between them than Sunderland alone had at this point in 2025. Régis Le Bris added a total of 18 new players to his squad last summer, with fellow promoted sides Burnley (15) and Leeds (11) also hitting double figures for incomings. By these standards, Ipswich (with seven new players), Hull (four) and Coventry (three) must recruit further.

At the opposite end of the Premier League scale, Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United have collectively spent two-thirds of a billion less on new talent than they did last summer. The latest rumour mill gossip says the champions may make a move for Vinícius Júnior. If not the Brazilian then perhaps Bradley Barcola, though Liverpool are also said to be pursuing the Paris Saint-Germain winger. Neither player will be remotely cheap. United are believed to be targeting Ollie Watkins – he wouldn’t cost Vinícius or Barcola money, but neither would Villa sell to a rival at a reduced fee.

The Premier League also has clubs who have yet to make an outlay. It is unlikely Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland end the summer without spending a transfer fee as is now the case. It would be remiss of Palace and Sunderland not to invest when they are in European competition this season. As for Forest, like Chelsea they have had an insatiable thirst for player turnover in recent times. With Elliot Anderson having left for an enormous fee, replacements will surely arrive soon.

It is remarkable to think the Premier League may not be halfway through its summer outlay when £1.4bn has already been used for recruitment. The top-flight English clubs collectively spent £3.1bn on players last summer, with over £600m in the final week of dealing alone. That figure may be blown away by the time the transfer window closes on 3 September.

Sports.title: Chelsea explore surprise moves for Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson
Sports.content:
Chelsea are understood to be in talks over a move to sign Danny Welbeck from Brighton. The 35-year-old is a surprise candidate to bolster Xabi Alonso’s forward line after scoring 13 goals in 37 Premier League matches last season.

In a further unexpected move, there are also reports the club are in negotiations to bring in England midfielder Jordan Henderson from Brentford. The 36-year-old has a year left on his contract, but it is claimed the Bees would be willing to let him leave on a free transfer.

The former Liverpool captain made 34 appearances for Brentford last season and was a member of England’s World Cup squad. He broke his arm when he fell over advertising hoardings celebrating their win over Mexico.

Welbeck also has a year remaining on his deal and there is optimism a deal can be concluded as Brighton are understood to be willing to let the striker move for the right price.

Should a deal be reached it would increase the likelihood of departures from Stamford Bridge, with uncertainty surrounding the futures of Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson. Delap is considered second-choice striker behind João Pedro, who impressed in his debut Chelsea campaign with 15 league goals, while Jackson spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich and has attracted interest from Aston Villa.

Delap had been expected to be given a second year to prove himself after an unsuccessful debut campaign following his £30m move from Ipswich a year ago, though this latest development would seem to cast doubt on his future.

Interest in Welbeck and Henderson reflects a revised Chelsea transfer policy as the club seek to recruit more established players under Alonso.

Welbeck, who scored twice when Brighton won 3-1 at Stamford Bridge last season, signed a 12-month deal in March which runs until the end of the 2026-27 season. If the move happens, Welbeck would join a long line of players and staff to make the switch from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years, including the goalkeeper Robert Sánchez, midfielder Moises Caicedo and striker João Pedro.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino could earn millions with ‘plans to sell stake in World Cup’ as UEFA issues damning statement
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino could earn millions with ‘plans to sell stake in World Cup’ as UEFA issues damning statement

Gianni Infantino is looking to sell World Cup stakes in a controversial move that could earn him millions, according to a report.

The FIFA president has spent a decade at the top of football's global governing body but looks set to cash in on it's biggest tournament.

3 Infantino is reportedly planning to sell World Cup stakes Credit: AFP

According to The Times, he plans to market stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

This would lead to the introduction of a new company that will be in charge of top competitions across men's and women's football.

The World Cup and Club World Cup would also come under control, and therefore expansion or more regular editions could materialise.

In addition, the plan is said to have been discussed with figures close to US president Donald Trump.

Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared is Trump's son-in-law, has been eyed as the primary investor candidate with the bank JP Morgan.

The plan would also see stakes worth around $20million (£15m) given to all of the 211 member associations involved with FIFA.

Once his last term as president concludes, which could be in 2031 at the earliest, Infantino would likely be the group's commissioner.

UEFA hit back at FIFA plans

Following the publication of The Times' article, the European football governing body released a statement to condemn the plan.

"This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," UEFA said.

"UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

3 Infantino could be in line for millions should he proceed Credit: Getty

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially.

"None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

Infantino under the spotlight

The 2026 World Cup was yet another spectacle on the pitch, but a series of controversies off it overshadowed the tournament.

Infantino has been the subject of intense scrutiny for his relationship with Trump, even before the World Cup began.

Trump was awarded the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize during the group stage draw in December.

He was championed by the FIFA president for 'unwavering commitment' to world peace through 'notable leadership and action'.

3 Infantino and his relationship with Trump has been a hot topic Credit: Getty

During the 2026 World Cup, United States striker Folarin Balogun had his one-match ban for a red card suspended for a year.

talkSPORT revealed that Trump called Infantino to review the decision, the only one of its kind out of all the 15 red card decisions.

In response, The Norwegian FA have intended to make a formal complaint to FIFA's ethics committee over Trump's intervention.

The red card has also been linked with potential betting irregularities.

On Monday, it was reported that a US lawmaker has requested for Infantino to appear before the House Judiciary Committee.

Rep. Jamie Raskin wants Infantino's relationship with Trump to be scrutinised and FIFA to provide all records of their contact with the politician.

Infantino has responded to the criticism aimed at him by accusing people of 'spreading hate'.

He called upon critics to instead 'reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match'.

Sports.title: English National League star joins Spanish club in unique role two months after signing new deal
Sports.content:
English National League star joins Spanish club in unique role two months after signing new deal

National League outfit Worthing have surprised fans by revealing Sam Beard has left the club two months after signing a new deal.

The club's vice-captain has completed a move to CD Atlético de Marbella Paraíso, which includes an academy coaching role.



2 Worthing boss Adam Hinshelwood will now have to replace his vice-captain Credit: Getty

The 28-year-old has made 200 appearances across the National League and National League South during his career.

The former Dorking, Barnet, and Eastbourne Borough player is now heading to Marbella to join a newly-promoted fifth-tier side.

The left-back has followed in the footsteps of his father, Mark Beard, who had a spell at Spanish lower league side San Pedro after his stints at the likes of Millwall, Sheffield United, and Southend.



National League star joins Spanish club in player/coach role

Former Brighton & Hove Albion youngster Beard was an integral part of Worthing's promotion to the National League last season.

‘Beardy’ started eight out of the club's final nine matches as the Mackerel Men were crowned National League South champions.



His manager Adam Hinshelwood - father of Brighton player Jack - was delighted to tie Beard down to a fresh contract in May.

“Beardy signing is a massive boost for us,” the 42-year-old revealed.

“He was a big part of our success towards the end of the season and is a player that has National League experience, which is going to be vital for our squad.”



Beard himself added: “I’m buzzing to extend my stay another year and play for this club in the National League.”

2 Beard (left) has left England to pursue the opportunity abroad Credit: Getty

However, two months later, Worthing confirmed an agreement has been reached with Atlético de Marbella Paraíso for Beard's transfer.

The Reds also revealed that alongside representing the Albicelestes as a player, their No.3 'will also work as a coach in their academy systems, contributing to several teams and age groups.'



Having helped return fifth-tier football to the Sussex Transport Community Stadium, Beard's new team achieved an identical promotion at the end of last season.

The phoenix club, who were born from the now defunct CA Marbella in 2010, will compete in the Tercera Federación this season for the first time in their existence.

Worthing, meanwhile, have already signed a new full-back this summer after agreeing a deal to loan QPR talent Cory Adjetey-Brew.

He joins fellow Queens Park Rangers teenager Harvey Boddy in spending the 2026/27 campaign with Hinshelwood's side.

Sports.title: Chelsea midfielder picks up 12th injury since joining in £58million deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea midfielder picks up 12th injury since joining in £58million deal

Romeo Lavia missed Chelsea's pre-season opener after Xabi Alonso confirmed the midfielder suffered from hamstring discomfort.

The majority of the Blues squad got valuable minutes under their belts during a 6-4 pre-season victory over Western Sydney Wanderers.



3 Lavia hasn't completed a full game for Chelsea since arriving from Southampton Credit: Getty

However, the 22-year-old was not among those involved having struggled for fitness ever since arriving from Southampton three years ago.

Recurring hamstring issues have limited the youngster to just 21 appearances for the west London outfit. Lavia is yet to complete 90 minutes in Chelsea colours.

The same problems resurfaced ahead of a pre-season match on Tuesday at the Accor Stadium in Sydney.



Speaking in his post-match press conference, Chelsea's new boss spoke on Lavia's status: "He felt something in the hamstring.

"Not a big thing. We are expecting him to be fit for Saturday, hopefully."



It is hoped that the player can return for the upcoming clash against Premier League rivals Tottenham Hotspur, which will also be played in Sydney.

However, Lavia's frustrating injury record may prompt the club to adopt a precautionary approach with him.



Prior to the match, Chelsea released a 'diary entry' from the player, reflecting on how he was feeling ahead of the new season.

He wrote: "We have all enjoyed working under the new manager, and he has great experience in the game.

"Pre-season so far has been about getting the basics in place to build on, because we want to have a great season.

3 Chelsea have spent over £200million in new signings since Alonso arrived Credit: Getty



"The manager was a great player, one of the best of his generation. You see that when he steps into a training session.

"He starts pinging balls around in a way only those who have played at the top level can. It’s a privilege to be working with him, especially as a midfielder.

"Personally, I’m feeling good. I did a lot of work with people at the club to ensure I was ready and could start pre-season strong once we got going.

"Now come the games, and we’re looking forward to getting out in front of the fans."



Meanwhile, Chelsea managed to navigate the contest with Western Sydney with no further injuries despite playing on a patchy pitch.

The venue had hosted three rugby league matches in the days leading up to the football clash.

3 Jorgensen has left Chelsea's pre-season tour amid growing transfer interest Credit: Getty

Lavia was not the only player absent from the travelling squad to not appear, with Filip Jorgensen, Jorrel Hato and Mamadou Sarr left out.



Jorgensen was on a flight back to Europe to finalise a transfer to the Blues' sister club, Strasbourg.

Meanwhile, Hato and Sarr were deemed too unfit to start and played no part in the match.

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini confirmed as new Italy boss – three years after resigning
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini confirmed as new Italy boss – three years after resigning

Italy have named Roberto Mancini as their new manager just three years after he stepped down from the role.

Mancini begins his second spell in charge of his nation following a five-year tenure from 2018 through to 2023.

3 Mancini has been named Italy manager again after winning the Euros in his last stint Credit: Getty

He led Italy to glory at the delayed Euro 2020 tournament, with his side beating Gareth Southgate's England on penalties at Wembley.

However, the former Manchester City manager also failed to qualify for the 2022 World Cup during his first stint as boss.

In total, Mancini took charge of 58 games with Italy - winning 38 matches and losing on just eight occasions.

Italy's main Man

Now, he returns - having been revealed by talkSPORT as a candidate in April - replacing Genaro Gattuso, who departed after his side missed out on the World Cup too.

Pep Guardiola was the first choice to take over from Gattuso, but he turned an approach down, opening the door for Mancini.

But the 61-year-old's appointment comes amid controversy within the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), which led to two resignations.

Italian icon Paolo Maldini quit his role as technical director alongside his advisor Leonardo after Andrea Pirlo was removed from the running to become the country's new manager.

Pirlo looked set to replace Gattuso, but due to his connection to a Russian betting company, the federation's president, Giovanni Malago, didn't want to appoint him.

That angered Maldini, who has now stepped down, with Malago going on to appoint Mancini instead of Pirlo.

He confirmed on Tuesday: "Mancini is the coach. I believed that the best person ​to become head coach was Roberto Mancini."

3 FIGC president Malago confirmed Mancini's appointment on Tuesday Credit: AFP

Why did Mancini resign in 2023?

Mancini resigned as Italy manager following a disagreement with the ex-FIGC president, Gabriele Gravina.

He did go on to thank Gravina in his leaving statement, which explained that his decision to leave his job was his own.

But the Premier League-winning boss eventually ended up revealing more details when speaking to an Italian newspaper.

Mancini said to La Repubblica: “Gravina had been trying for a year to revolutionise my staff. I tried to tell him that at most he could add a couple of new faces, but he couldn’t take away two members of a group that works and had won.

"If anything, it should be me who decides to substitute a member of my staff.

“Gravina had for a while thought about things very differently from me. I was massacred purely for my decision. I wanted to send a signal to the President, he could’ve helped me if he had wanted to.”

3 Ranieri has replaced Maldini as technical director with Italy too Credit: Getty

Maldini replacement

As well as appointing Mancini, Italy have also replaced Maldini following his resignation as technical director.

Legendary Italian manager Claudio Ranieri has been handed the role, with Malago explaining his decision to bring him in.

"I needed someone with whom I could share the decision on the coach, because without that shared view my reasoning would ⁠have ​carried little weight," the FIGC president said.

"So consequently, today we have ​a new coach and a new technical director for Italy."

Ranieri's last managerial role was with Roma in Serie A in 2025, with the 74-year-old now taking a behind-the-scenes position.

Italy's first fixture with their new, experienced faces involved will be on September 25 as they face Turkey in the Nations League.

Sports.title: European club face six-month exile from stadium amid ‘serious’ safety concerns
Sports.content:
Executives will redevelop the Vallecas Stadium, home of Spanish side Rayo Vallecano, after detecting serious safety concerns.

Rayo are at risk of not being able to play at their home ground in the upcoming LaLiga season, which begins on August 14, until 2027.

3 Rayo's stadium is in need of renovation due to worrying safety issues Credit: Getty

The Government of the Community of Madrid have ownership of the 14,708-capacity stadium as the area's local collegiate organisation.

Spanish outlet Diario AS say they have issued a termination of the club's concession agreement, which allows Rayo to operate there.

A 'precautionary suspension measure' has been introduced, meaning the club cannot play at the Vallecas Stadium.

'Serious safety deficiencies' are said to have been discovered as part of an audit carried out in October ahead of proposed renovations.

Aspects of the stadium that relate to hygiene, sanitation and health are deemed to be unsafe, with fire protection also a concern.

Images shared on social media show discarded items and rubbish in the vicinity of the stadium.

Mariano de Paco, the Minister of Culture, Tourism and Sports for the Community of Madrid, couldn't give a definite timeline for the work.

"We don't know if it will be two or six months," he said. "But we will keep you updated in real time on what we are doing."

The stadium renovation is reportedly set to begin on Wednesday.

Plans include adding 4,000 new seats, an extra stand and a multi-purpose tower in a view to host other events including concerts.

3 Rayo may have to wait until 2027 to return to their ground Credit: Getty

As it stands, Rayo will not be able to host Deportivo Alaves in their league match on August 20.

Home fixtures against Racing de Santander and RCD Espanyol are also set to be affected, as per the two month minimum timeframe.

It is not yet clear as to which stadium Rayo will call their temporary base for 'home' fixtures.

Rayo risk turbulent season

It's hard to believe that a club who reached last season's Conference League final are in such a predicament before the new campaign.

Rayo finished fourth in the league phase of Europe's third-tier tournament and narrowly lost 1-0 to Crystal Palace in the showpiece.

They also just missed out on qualification for Europe via their LaLiga position as they ended the season in eighth.

3 Rayo have played at their stadium since 1976 Credit: Getty

Inigo Perez has left as manager, having previously been assistant to new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola before taking the job himself.

Benat San Jose was announced as his replacement and is tasked with navigating a difficult start to the new season.

Rayo travel to Sevilla on the opening weekend before facing Alaves at a venue that is currently unknown.

They then travel to the reigning champions Barcelona at the end of August, with Real Madrid also an opponent in mid-September.

Rayo could be set to play these fixtures without key player Pep Chavarria, who made 44 appearances last season.

Chelsea have been in advanced talks over a move for the left-back this summer.

Sports.title: Sean Dyche clarifies comment that new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola plays ‘lower league football’
Sports.content:
Sean Dyche has revealed his claim that Andoni Iraola plays 'lower league football' was meant as a compliment.

The former Nottingham Forest boss faced backlash for comments that emerged this week when discussing Iraola's Bournemouth side on a recent podcast.

4 Dyche has clarified comments he made claiming Iraola plays 'lower league football' Credit: Getty

Dyche had reflected on the turnaround the Spaniard produced during the first of his three seasons with the Cherries.

Iraola was appointed as Bournemouth manager in the summer of 2023, but failed to win any of his first nine Premier League matches.

He began his tenure with just one victory in his opening 11 league outings, including a 3-0 loss to Dyche's Everton in October 2023.

However, Iraola has since won all four meetings with Dyche since and improved on Bournemouth's previous league finish in each of his three seasons as manager.

Those culminated with a record-high sixth place last term to qualify for the Europa League for the first time in their history.

Iraola has since left the club to take charge at Liverpool, with Marco Rose replacing him as Bournemouth boss.

What did Dyche say?

Despite his success on the south coast, Dyche claimed Iraola played 'lower league football' during an appearance on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast.

The talkSPORT co-host explained: "Iraola basically plays lower league football, but at a high level.

"They turn you and turn you, and force you into submission. High quality and high energy version."

Turning his attention to Bournemouth's transformation under Iraola, he added: "I marvelled at it because we ran all over them at Everton when he was trying to play what you would imagine is the Spanish way.

4 Iraola guided Bournemouth to Europa League qualification last term before becoming Liverpool head coach Credit: Getty

"I think he is brilliant at managing, as you could tell he went 'this ain't going to work'.

"The next time we played them, he is bombing it down our throats, getting us turned, full-backs keep turning and having to run back towards their own goal, centre halves thinking that they never get a break. They looked a different outfit and he's done a brilliant job."

'Massive compliment' - Dyche

Following claims the former Burnley boss was aiming a dig at Iraola, Dyche clarifies his remarks on Tuesday.

Speaking to Jonny Owen live on talkSPORT, he heaped praise on Iraola's Bournemouth side, admitting: "The stories are coming back out now, almost making out that I was doing him down by saying he played high-level lower league football.

"It was a massive compliment, I didn’t mean it in that way and they know I didn’t because I always said it as a compliment.

"There’s nothing wrong with getting the ball forward, they do it with real ability, players have a very high ability.

4 Iraola has won his last four meetings with Dyche since losing the first match between their sides Credit: Getty

"Some of those Bournemouth players are ever so underrated, well they’re not so much now, and lifting it behind teams, asking questions, wide players running at teams, putting teams under pressure, pressing from the off.

"Like a variant of a 4-4-2, two midfielders working their socks off, doing all the ugly hard yards, but with some ability as well.

"(Antoine) Semenyo, what a season he had. Now whether they can do it again now that the manager has changed would be a different thing."

As for whether Iraola could implement the same approach at Liverpool, Dyche added: "But I wonder whether Iraola is going to take that thinking into a Liverpool camp, which to be fair it’s not that dissimilar to the end of (Jurgen) Klopp’s (reign).

"Playing a lot of longer passes, a lot more quality longer passes because as soon as I say that people think I’m doing them down. I’m not, I’m complimenting these players.

"If you’re a Premier League player and you can’t pass it 30 or 40 yards, you shouldn’t be a Premier League player.

4 Dyche explained his remarks were meant as a compliment as he responded on talkSPORT Credit: talkSPORT

"So there’s nothing wrong with a longer pass and I think Iraola will use that wisely, particularly with a higher level.

"Even more higher level than the Bournemouth players have proved to be."

Sports.title: Liverpool pre-season star not allowed to play for Andoni Iraola this season
Sports.content:
Liverpool pre-season star not allowed to play for Andoni Iraola this season

Liverpool have been dealt a blow with highly-rated defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe blocked from playing a minute for the club this season.

The 18-year-old impressed on his unofficial Reds debut, featuring in the 4-2 pre-season win over Sunderland last weekend.

3 Ndukwe showcased his potential in Nashville as Liverpool beat Sunderland Credit: Getty

The centre-back completed a £2.6million move from Austria Vienna at the start of the year but didn't officially arrive until this summer.

Ndukwe was snapped up by Liverpool in January alongside fellow teenager Mor Talla Ndiaye following the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar.

The pair were then tasked with forming a defensive partnership for Andoni Iraola's first match after Joe Gomez suffered an early injury.

Liverpool's defensive injury issues

Liverpool are already down to the bare bones at the back, with captain Virgil van Dijk on an extended break following the World Cup.

The 35-year-old has played more minutes for club and country than any other player in Europe's top five leagues since June 2025.

His ex-centre-back partner Ibrahima Konate has already left on a free transfer to Real Madrid, with Gomez now sustaining another injury.

Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from a torn anterior cruciate ligament that he sustained on his Liverpool debut last September.

Meanwhile, new signing Jeremy Jacquet was also left out of the squad against Sunderland due to concerns over a shoulder issue.

However, Ndukwe won't have the opportunity to stake a claim to be an immediate part of Iraola's plans regardless of how well he plays.

3 Gomez's injury opened the door for Ndukwe to make his unofficial Reds debut Credit: Getty

Why Ndukwe cannot play for Liverpool this season

As per the Athletic, the Austria youth international doesn’t meet the required points total to get a work permit in the UK.

Before Brexit in January 2020, Ndukwe would have been able to qualify for such a permit due to his country being part of the EU.

But now, Liverpool will have little choice but to send Ndukwe out on loan for the 2026/27 campaign for him to get first-team football.

The Reds are currently based in the USA for the start of their pre-season, with upcoming matches against Wrexham and Leeds United.

Ndukwe will be available to appear in both of these friendlies, but won't be included for the Premier League opener away at Newcastle.

3 Ndukwe did not officially make the switch to Anfield until June Credit: Getty

What are the Premier League work permit rules?

England's top-flight and EFL clubs know that any player signed from overseas must qualify for a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE).

The points-based system determines eligibility using a number of factors, including the quality of the league they were playing in before and their experience at both club and international level.

Players with 15 points or more are granted work permits, with those with 10-14 points subject to appeal.

Anyone with fewer than 10 points can be signed but can't play; such was the case when £50million Manchester United star Andrey Santos first joined Chelsea, but returned on loan to Vasco da Gama.

In Liverpool's case, Ndukwe has only made one first-team appearance in the Austrian league, which sits 20th in UEFA's coefficient ranking.

He is also yet to earn a senior international cap, having only played three times for his country's Under-19 team.

Sports.title: Village cricket cheating scandal convulses Middle England as 'Clicky Ponting' fielder's trick fools umpires
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

An amateur village cricket team is at the centre of a cheating scandal that has gone viral across the world after one of their fielders was accused of tricking umpires by clicking his fingers to imitate the noise of an edge off the bat.

An investigation has been launched by the North Yorkshire and South Durham League into the cheating allegations against Saltburn Cricket Club after video footage emerged online.

In the footage shared widely online, Saltburn's first slip appears to fool the umpires by clicking his fingers to get the batsman out.

Now the Daily Mail can reveal the cricketer at the centre of the storm is 'legendary' amateur player Brian Devine.

Mr Devine, 38, has played for years at Saltburn Cricket Club and is well known on the cricket scene in North Yorkshire.

A prolific batsman, he also previously played for Pudsey St Lawrence Cricket Club, helping them to win the Bradford Premier League second tier championship in 2023.

Following this achievement, he returned to Saltburn for the start of the 2024 season, with one social media post noting: 'Excellent batting on Saturday from returning legend Brian Devine. 95 runs.'

There was such excitement about his return that he even managed to secure a sponsorship deal with local Indian restaurant Spices of Saltburn.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his actions on the cricket field

Saltburn player has been caught on camera clicking his fingers whenever ball was near bat

Norton batsman Noman Shabir protested that he didn't touch the ball after being given out

Mr Devoine, a father-of-one, from Guisborough, Cleveland, works as a company secretary at Northallerton Auctions, which specialises in auctions for livestock and farm machinery.

When contacted about the viral video by the Daily Mail, and told he had been identified as 'Clicky Ponting', Brian responded 'Naturally I can't comment on that.'

Then when told he was being widely accused of cheating, and asked whether there was some other explanation for what takes place in the videos, he said: 'I don't want to talk about it. I'm at work.'

From his social media posts, in addition to his obvious love for cricket, Brian also appears to be a big fan of Boris Johnson.

In one post from 2022 he wrote: 'Top man Boris. Others may try to put you down! I won't have a bad word said! I am off to get my kettle.'

The accused cricketer's mother-in-law today told the Mail he is a 'man of integrity.'

Georgina Vaughan, the mother of Devine's partner Clare, said the family had been shocked by the scale of the cheating row.

She said: 'It was only a little village cricket match and now it's become this thing that's all over the news and social media.

'It has got totally out of hand and there is nothing that any of us want to say.'

Asked whether Devine was a man of integrity, she replied: 'He certainly is.'

Footage from Saltburn's 2nd XI match with Norton Cricket Club in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League last weekend showed a ball delivered by Saltburn bowler Sam Morrison passing the bat of Norton batsman Noman Shabir without making contact with it.

At the same time, Mr Devine playing at first slip seems to click his fingers.

When Saltburn wicketkeeper Josh Bowes takes the ball, Saltburn appeal and the umpire gives Shabir out.

Shabir can clearly be seen objecting to his dismissal and seems to indicate to the umpire that he did not hit the ball and that the noise heard was a clicking of fingers instead.

The clip and other similar evidence have attracted international media attention and gone viral online and on social media.

A statement from the North Yorkshire and South Durham League read: 'The League has received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday 25th July 2026. A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete, no further comment will be made.'

Saltburn won their match with Norton by a mammoth 159 runs.

Devine has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' - in a light-hearted reference to Australia legend Ricky Ponting.

That's as far as the funny side goes though with the likes of Piers Morgan condemning the actions.

Taking to X, the avid cricket fan wrote: 'Outrageous cheating, and just the tip of the iceberg from all that's come out since it was exposed.

'Clicky Ponting (as he is now known) and various teammates at Saltburn CC, have clearly been at this shameful scam for years. Imagine doing this in local amateur cricket? Pathetic.'

Other clips online appear to show Devine clicking his fingers to cheat umpires and earn dismissals unfairly in other matches.

One such example is a video showing footage of a match between Saltburn and Middlesbrough second XI.

Outrageous cheating, and just the tip of the iceberg from all that’s come out since it was exposed. Clicky Ponting (as he is now known) and various teammates at Saltburn CC, have clearly been at this shameful scam for years. Imagine doing this in local amateur cricket? Pathetic. https://t.co/fFOusuys4u — Piers Morgan (@piersmorgan) July 28, 2026

Other incidences have been found of Devine clicking his finger in previous matches for wickets

The North Yorkshire and South Durham League have begin a full investigation into Saltburn

Saltburn have been widely-condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

The actions of Saltburn have been described as 'the worst case of cheating' seen in cricket online, with it likely that long bans will be handed out. Unconfirmed reports online suggested that Devine has already been suspended for the rest of the season by Saltburn. Daily Mail Sport approached both Saltburn and Norton for comment but did not receive a reply.

In 13 matches across 2026 with Devine as the slip catcher, Saltburn's wicket-keeper has taken 39 catches. In seven matches without Devine, the wicket-keeper has taken just five.

In addition to the numerous video clips seemingly showing Devine clicking his fingers online, further suspicion over Saltburn's antics has been aroused by the scorecards of previous matches.

On July 18, Saltburn's second XI played Shildon Railway CC with wicketkeeper Bowes taking a mammoth eight catches. Such a number is highly unusual. The record number of dismissals for a wicketkeeper in a Test match innings is seven. Bowes is averaging almost four catches per match in eight games this season. The investigation remains ongoing.

It is the responsibility of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League to investigate any allegations of cheating or complaints over the behaviour of teams as well as imposing any sanctions. As such, it is unlikely that at this stage the England & Wales Cricket Board – as English cricket's governing body – will get involved directly.

Sports.title: Newcastle insist Arsenal have NOT made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap... and Ajax want return for West Ham's Edson Alvarez: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Tomiyasu training with Palace

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is training with Crystal Palace after the expiry of his contract at Ajax.

The Japan international was expected to extend his contract but is a free agent after making just nine appearances since moving to Amsterdam on a short-term deal in January owing in part to a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old is training with Palace in Como as part of the club’s pre-season preparations and could feature in a friendly this week. He has had interest from Venezia and Sassuolu, too.

Palace are playing in the Como Cup. They face Lens, new manager Pierre Sage's former side, tonight then take on Famalicao in two 45-minute games.

Takehiro Tomiyasu

Bees eye Sarr signing

Brentford are weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

The Bees were looking to strengthen their options even before news of Jordan Henderson's proposed departure for Chelsea.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabate from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future. They now want two more for the first team squad with Henderson heading towards Stamford Bridge.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Pape Matar Sarr is on Brentford's radar, with Jordan Henderson wanted by Chelsea

Newcastle still waiting on Arsenal bid for Bruno

Newcastle United insist they have still to receive a formal approach from Arsenal for midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing to make an official £70m-plus move for the Brazilian who is keen to join them but, so far, Newcastle sources say any proposals have come via the player's agent.

Newcastle manager Eddie Howe said at the weekend he was unsure what would happen over the 28-year-old's future.

Bruno Guimaraes wants to move to Arsenal but Newcastle say they are still waiting for a bid

Delap in demand with Chelsea set to sign Welbeck

Nottingham Forest remain among the list of clubs showing interest in Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Danny Welbeck's pending arrival from Brighton is likely to leave fewer opportunities for 22-year-old Delap and clubs are enquiring to ascertain the deal required to sign the former Ipswich Town forward.

Forest, Everton and Newcastle United are just some of the clubs who have expressed interest in the former England U21 international.

Meanwhile, Forest have made an offer for Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili as talks for Feyenoord's Givairo Read also continue.

Both players are also appreciated by Bournemouth and Newcastle United.

Liam Delap is a target for several clubs with his chances at Chelsea likely to be limited

Jorgensen leaves camp for France

Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen has left their camp in Australia ahead of joining sister club Strasbourg.

The 24-year-old Denmark international made 12 appearances for Chelsea last season and wants regular first team football.

On my Edson! Ajax want West Ham's Alvarez back

Ajax are trying to re-sign West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Dutch side sold Alvarez to West Ham for £35million in 2023 and now hope to buy him back.

West Ham want around £12.5m but Ajax sources say they are still owed money from the way payment was structured on the original transfer.

The 28-year-old, who has spoken to Ajax director Jordi Cruyff, spent last season on loan at Fenerbahce and was part of Mexico's World Cup squad but has generally struggled to live up to expectations since leaving Amsterdam.

Real Sociedad are also interested in Alvarez but are proposing a smaller, structured deal.

Edson Alvarez in action for Mexico against England at the World Cup

Rock on Tommi to Meadow Lane

Aston Villa winger Tommi O'Reilly is in talks to join League One Notts County on loan.

The 22-year-old had been set to sign for Sheffield Wednesday but, after further discussions, Villa have decided Meadow Lane may suit his development better.

O'Reilly had an outstanding campaign with Crewe last season and Villa hope he can replicate that form under Notts County coach Martin Paterson.

Notts County also signed Australian forward Luka Smyth from Finnish top-flight side VPS yesterday for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.

Notts County are in talks over a deal for Villa's Tommi O'Reilly

Perri set for Italian job after Trafford deal

Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri is expected to join Torino on loan with an option to buy once a deal for James Trafford is completed.

Trafford, 23, is poised to sign a deal worth around £130,000 a week once Manchester City and Leeds finalise details on an expected £40m transfer with £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Torino and Leeds have agreed an initial loan move for Perri for the coming season. The deal also includes an option to buy him permanently next summer.

Leeds goalkeepers Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier have left Daniel Farke’s squad to join Manchester United and Arsenal this summer.

They would still like another as cover as well as strengthening at left-back, attacking midfield and striker.

Lucas Perri's Torino deal may be signed off after James Trafford arrives from Manchester City
