Sports.title: UEFA lay into FIFA over 'proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup' in a move that could 'make president Gianni Infantino millions' - as plan is labelled a 'nuclear bomb' for football
Sports.content:
UEFA have hit out at FIFA's proposed plans to sell stakes in the World Cup in a move that could make their president Gianni Infantino millions.

News broke in The Times on Tuesday afternoon that FIFA President Infantino was reportedly considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that may be worth around £15billion.

The report added that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, moving him into a highly lucrative position that estimates suggest may pay him more than $50million-a-year.

The bank JPMorgan is said to be handling the process and the Donald Trump administration are understood to have been consulted.

The proposal has already received widespread criticism from across football, with one source telling The Times it would be a 'nuclear bomb' for the sport and another arguing it would 'potentially be much worse than the European Super League'.

And UEFA, who have been critical of FIFA and Infantino's actions in recent times, hit out at their counterparts.

FIFA are reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup in a hugely contentious move

UEFA launched a strongly worded statement slamming plans that 'crossed a line' (pictured - UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin)

'This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,' they said in a statement. 'UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association.

'So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.'

If the move was to go ahead, the global football calendar would likely be affected.

For example, the Men's and Women's World Cup may be expanded or held more regularly than every four years, while the Club World Cup could face similar changes.

As part of the proposal, all 211 member associations would have stakes that would make up 20 per cent of the total company and be worth around $20million (£15million) each.

That is a larger figure than many of their annual revenues, and they would be given the option to sell them to raise funds.

FIFA would retain a majority stake in the new entity and private investors would be able to take on minority stakes.

Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, was reported to be one of the potential investors

FIFA are a not-for-profit organisation and enjoy tax-free status at their HQ in Switzerland.

For the most recent cycle of 2022-2026, their revenue is expected to be around $15billion (£11.3billion) – much of which came from this summer's World Cup – meaning this would provide a lucrative opportunity for individuals to be involved in.

The Times added that the blueprint for the potential selling of stakes has been discussed among senior FIFA figures and potential investors, which could include Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared – and they have signed non-disclosure agreements.

Some of those potential investors are understood to have even spoken internally about 'buying FIFA'.

The reports come at a time when Infantino is already under fire for a variety of reasons following the World Cup.

This includes the US visa restrictions that affected supporters and officials from many countries, the extremely high prices of tickets and Infantino's links with Trump, which came to a head after Folarin Balogun's red card was suspended following a phone call by the US President to the Swiss administrator.

When contacted for comment, FIFA confirmed plans to launch a new body called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which they described as a 'controlled subsidiary consolidating FIFA's commercial and event operations'.

They added that 'FIFA would retain sole control of FFE and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions,' and claimed the move would increase the funding available to all 211 member associations.

The Daily Mail Sport also contacted the White House for comment.

Sports.title: County cricket transfers: Sussex finally land first signing under ECB sanctions, England star signs new Durham deal, the issue holding up James Vince's Hampshire contract and Gloucestershire snap up Indian spinner
Sports.content:
County cricket transfers: Sussex finally land first signing under ECB sanctions, England star signs new Durham deal, the issue holding up James Vince's Hampshire contract and Gloucestershire snap up Indian spinner

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Sussex have signed Joey Evison on a multi-year deal from 2027 in a landmark move ratified by the ECB.

Under the spending restrictions the ECB placed upon Sussex for recording an operating loss of £1.33million last year, county cricket’s managing director Rob Andrew must approve new player signings at Hove until the end of the 2028 season.

Evison is the first arrival of this period, having found chances to play in his favoured role increasingly limited at Kent, partly due to the emergence of another ex-England Under 19s all-rounder in Ekansh Singh. In his two most recent County Championship appearances for the club, Evison was carded at No 8, the same position he occupied in the one-day loss to Gloucestershire on Sunday.

The 24-year-old is leaving Kent with a year remaining on his contract after a deal was struck that is financially favourable to both clubs.

Viewing batting as the stronger of his two suits, he went on loan to Leicestershire last month, striking 55 in the innings win over Yorkshire and claiming combined figures of three for 87 across two appearances.

Evison was touted as one of the country’s brightest prospects when Kent signed him from Nottinghamshire four years ago and some supporters will be disappointed that a player with 14 half centuries in 45 first-class appearances at an average of 31.65 is departing the club early.

Sussex have signed Kent all-rounder Joey Evison, who had to go on loan to Leicestershire this month after being unable to get into the team

The 24-year-old won man of the match in the 2022 One-Day Cup final as Kent beat Lancashire at Trent Bridge

He also has 68 wickets at 43 and two Metro Bank Cup hundreds on his CV, winning man of the match in the 2022 final when Kent beat Lancashire at Trent Bridge.

The move reunites him with his former Kent coach Matt Walker, who is taking over from Paul Farbrace at Sussex next season. With all-rounders Fynn Hudson-Prentice, who is joining Hampshire, and Danny Lamb among those leaving the club in the next few weeks, opportunities should be plentiful.

Sussex are also in talks to add Middlesex seamer Blake Cullen to a group that will be without Tom Alsop in 2027 after a deal was struck with Gloucestershire. Daily Mail Sport first flagged the potential move for the left-hander in April, when it was announced Ben Charlesworth would be swapping Bristol for Lancashire next year.

Alsop, 30, had 12 months remaining on his deal with Sussex and will continue to live in Hove, but is moving early on a three-year deal having been limited to two Division One outings this summer due to the form of Tom Clark at No 3.

Sussex have already lost rising fast bowling star Henry Crocombe to Surrey, a signing that concluded a scramble among Test-hosting counties. Yorkshire and Nottinghamshire also went in strongly for the 24-year-old, who was called into England’s second Test squad against New Zealand last month as cover for county team-mate Ollie Robinson.

A knock-on of that business was James Taylor agreeing to leave Surrey for Yorkshire, scuppering Worcestershire’s plan to pair him with his brother Tom in a new-look new-ball attack next season. Somerset, Gloucestershire and Glamorgan were also interested.

Potts stays put

Daily Mail Sport understands Matthew Potts has committed his future to Durham beyond September following enquiries from Yorkshire.

The Sunderland-born England seamer, 27, is looking to regain his place in the national team after a tricky Ashes last winter Down Under.

Daily Mail Sport understands Matthew Potts has committed his future to Durham beyond September following enquiries from Yorkshire

Patterson-White is Notts for sale

Another north-easterner in Liam Patterson-White is also staying put with Nottinghamshire, signing a three-year contract after listening to an offer from Warwickshire, who failed to replace the experienced Danny Briggs when he returned to Sussex last winter.

Slow left-armer Patterson-White is comfortably the most prolific spin bowler across the Championship’s two divisions this summer, with 32 wickets at under 24 runs each.

Midlands battle for keeper Cox

Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire are understood to be contesting the capture of 34-year-old wicketkeeper Ben Cox, who is leaving Leicestershire in September.

Only the Hampshire-bound Rishi Patel has scored more top-flight runs for the Foxes than the 530 contributed by Cox in 2026.

Shaikh up at Leicestershire

Leicestershire have made an investment for the future by snapping up Warwickshire’s ex-England Under 19s captain Hamza Shaikh on a three-year contract from 2027, while spinner Liam Trevaskis’ future at Grace Road remains uncertain.

Hampshire eye new deals for key batsmen

One soon-to-be free agent whose negotiating position has improved significantly in recent weeks, though, is Hampshire batsman Joe Weatherley, the most prolific run-scorer in this year’s T20 Blast.

While Ali Orr is expected to leave the Utilita Bowl for Middlesex, Weatherley enjoys working with coach Russell Domingo and is understood to be keen to stay, particularly if his preference to bat lower down the order in four-day cricket is met.

Hampshire’s T20 captain James Vince is finalising a new deal with the club that is complicated not by financial demands, but the limited number of days he is permitted to work in the UK now that he is a resident of the United Arab Emirates for tax purposes.

Hampshire batsman Joe Weatherley enjoys working with coach Russell Domingo and is understood to be keen to stay

Indian duo snapped up

With the Championship returning in three weeks, counties have turned their attention for recruitment for the season finale, with Yorkshire securing India’s left-arm wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav for three September fixtures following a five-match Metro Bank Cup stint, and Gloucestershire welcoming his compatriot Ravi Sai Kishore - who bagged 11 wickets in two matches for Surrey last year - for the final six rounds.

Gloucestershire are rooted to the foot of the Division Two table, 43 points behind second-bottom Lancashire, but director of cricket Jon Lewis says the arrival of Sai Kishore is an indication of their desire to avoid the wooden spoon.

Who'll Toole up for 2027?

One other potential signing for this period of the campaign is Ray Toole, the left-armer who was the leading wicket-taker in New Zealand’s Plunket Shield last winter.

Toole, 28, previously played for Essex and Durham and is known to be of interest to several counties for 2027. However, with the crammed county schedule affording just two-day gaps between first-class matches, he could yet be snapped up on a shorter-term deal covering this August and September.

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane is announced as France's new manager on a four-year-deal - as football icon succeeds former team-mate Didier Deschamps
Sports.content:
Zinedine Zidane has been announced as France's new manager, with the long-expected announcement having finally been delivered.

The 54-year-old has signed a four-year deal with Les Bleus as he succeeds his former Juventus and France team-mate Didier Deschamps.

Deschamps left his 14-year tenure as France manager at the end of the World Cup, with his side losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain in the semi-finals. They finished fourth after a 6-4 defeat by England in the third-place play-off.

Zidane's unveiling took place on Tuesday morning at the French Football Federation's (FFF) headquarters in Paris, alongside FFF president Philippe Diallo.

It is Zidane's first foray back into management since leaving Real Madrid in 2021, revealing he has rejected offers in the meantime as he waited for his 'dream' to become France boss.

'The French team was the only thing I wanted to do,' Zidane told reporters.

Zinedine Zidane has been announced as France's new manager on a four-year contract

He revealed he has rejected club management roles as he waited for his 'dream' job instead

Zidane succeeds Didier Deschamps (centre) who bowed out at the end of the World Cup

'I've always looked at this team through the eyes of a future manager. I didn't take a club job for that reason. The only thing I wanted to do after Madrid was manage the French national team.

'I could have taken on a three-year role because Deschamps was there. He made that decision in January 2025, and the very next day I knew I wanted to be the next one. We met with the president and the deal was sealed.'

Deschamps oversaw 185 matches and 120 victories, guiding France to the 2018 World Cup title, the 2020-21 Nations League trophy, and the Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup finals.

He and Zidane share a long association, having been team-mates in France's 1998 World Cup-winning side on home soil.

Zidane played a pivotal role in that triumph and won the Ballon d'Or that year. He made 108 appearances for the national side, scoring 31 goals and contributing 29 assists.

'You'll see my [team's] style soon,' Zidane said. 'I'm driven by the game. I was a No 10, and what drives me is scoring goals.

'I lived in Spain for 25 years, you know what that means. On the pitch, I was a leader. Now I'm becoming a leader through my experience.

'Winning in '98 is the best thing that's ever happened to me, winning with my team-mates. I spent those four or five years waiting for that day. I'm emotional; you can't see it, but I'm so excited. I'm happy.'

The pair were team-mates at Juventus and France as players (pictured for Les Bleus in 2000)

Speaking about Zidane's arrival, Diallo revealed that negotiations with the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000 winner began in February 2025 after Deschamps said he would stand down after the 2026 World Cup.

'This is an exceptional moment, exceptional because of the person sat next to me,' Diallo said. 'Zinedine is one of the legends of French soccer and for many years he said one of his dreams was to take charge of the France team.'

'I would like to thank Didier Deschamps and his staff for their work. For 14 years he led the France team to the top.'

The length of the deal means Zidane will work through until at least the 2030 World Cup, incorporating two Nations Leagues (2026-27 and 2028-29) as well as Euro 2028 before the major showpiece.

His first match in the hotseat will be away to Türkiye in the Nations League on September 25. After that comes a trip to local rivals Belgium on September 28 with a clash against Italy on October 2 sparking his first game in charge on home soil.

Sports.title: Nine-minute hat-trick hero Joao Pedro is 'very hungry' after Brazil World Cup snub, says Xabi Alonso - as Chelsea boss opens up on Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson pursuits
Sports.content:
Nine-minute hat-trick hero Joao Pedro is 'very hungry' after Brazil World Cup snub, says Xabi Alonso - as Chelsea boss opens up on Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson pursuits

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Xabi Alonso described Joao Pedro as ‘very hungry’ after Chelsea’s striker scored a nine-minute hat-trick in Sydney, having been left at home by Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti for the World Cup.

The 24-year-old was surprisingly ignored by Ancelotti this summer, and in a friendly win over Western Sydney Wanderers, he replaced Liam Delap while his side were trailing 3-2.

Joao Pedro assisted Jamie Gittens for the equaliser before scoring three times himself for a 6-4 victory.

‘He is very hungry,’ Alonso said when asked about Joao Pedro being snubbed by Brazil. ‘Joao is really, really determined to have a great season. He wants to keep scoring more and more.

'We need to help him. On his own it's not possible. He will have the players around him. It’s not just about the striker, but every time we win and our striker scores, I am happy.’

On Delap, who could leave this summer to make way for Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old at Brighton who Daily Mail Sport revealed is a transfer target, Alonso added: ‘I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football, feeling good, and he's doing well.’

Joao Pedro scored a hat-trick as Chelsea beat Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 in pre-season

Blues boss Xabi Alonso said the striker is 'very hungry' after missing the World Cup with Brazil

Asked about wanting to add experience, with Chelsea looking at Welbeck and Brentford midfielder Jordan Henderson, 36, Alonso said: ‘Everyone has to learn. Everyone. It doesn't matter if you are young, if you are more experienced, this is what happens in the game.

‘This is a quality as well that you need. You can be quick. You can be good at dribbling. But you can have this game intelligence to do the things and from everything we need to be quick because the competition is in just almost a month and we want to get ready for that.

‘We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team. For that we have an idea, we have a plan, and let's see how we set it up until the start of the Premier League.’

Asked specifically about Welbeck, Alonso said: ‘No comment.’

Romeo Lavia received no minutes in this friendly because of a minor hamstring issue. In his place, 16-year-old Reggie Watson was the only player to complete a full 90 for Chelsea, and the son of former Crystal Palace and Wigan footballer Ben impressed in the centre.

As did Dastan Satpayev, the 17-year-old who arrived this summer from Kazakhstan side FC Kairat. ‘He is really strong, really quick, and you will be really impressed with him,’ Alonso said.

Sports.title: Liam Delap edging towards exit after struggling in Sydney as Nottingham Forest circle, the 16-year-old who wowed Xabi Alonso and the forgotten man battling for starting spot: Chelsea 6-4 Western Sydney TAKEAWAYS
Sports.content:
Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen travelled all the way from England to Australia, only to return home after three days in Sydney because he is in line to leave the club, most likely for BlueCo sister side Strasbourg.

Liam Delap has not been sent home, though the striker could be sold this summer to make way for Danny Welbeck, 35. Nottingham Forest are among Delap’s admirers, though the 23-year-old’s inclusion in Xabi Alonso’s starting line-up in the 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers suggested no move is imminent.

If this was a chance for Delap to convince Alonso that he should veto any switch which may crop up, he did not take it. The £30million signing from Ipswich last summer was upstaged by Chelsea’s other attackers in this friendly, and not least the man who replaced him in Joao Pedro.

Delap took his seat in the dugout after an hour, and the difference between him leading the line and Joao Pedro was stark. The 24-year-old Brazilian just looked a level above.

In the 66th minute, he produced a sublime assist for Jamie Gittens after squirming his way into the box. In the 80th, he scored his first goal. In the 85th, he scored his second. In the 89th, he confirmed his hat-trick.

It is no wonder Chelsea let it be known early on this summer that Joao Pedro is considered untouchable. Of course Barcelona like him. Every club in Europe should consider him an improvement on what they already have. That is only natural. But he is going nowhere – whereas Delap might be.

Joao Pedro ran the game after coming on in the 66th minute

Liam Delap took his seat in the dugout after an hour, and the difference between him leading the line and Joao Pedro was stark

Teen dreams

Two 17-year-olds in Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Dastan Satpayev combined for the first of Chelsea’s six goals here.

It involved a lovely turn and through-ball from Kavuma-McQueen for Satpayev, whose finish was clinical after breaking behind.

Satpayev is technically not a Chelsea player until he turns 18 next month, but he was involved here as a ‘trialist’, with permission from his club FC Kairat in Kazakhstan and authorisation from his parents.

Reggie Walsh, 17, impressed at No 10 as he exchanged a one-two with Dario Essugo for Chelsea’s second goal. Landon Emenalo, 18, was flying down the flank from left back also.

This was a good opportunity for the kids, and the best of the bunch, in my opinion, was Reggie Watson. Still only 16 and the son of former Wigan midfielder Ben, Watson was a physical force in midfield.

When Alonso made nine substitutes after an hour, he was the only starter who remained on the pitch, and it is easy to see why Chelsea are so excited by this teenager.

Still only 16 and the son of former Wigan midfielder Ben, Reggie Watson was a physical force in midfield

Dastan Satpayev is technically not a Chelsea player until he turns 18 next month, but he was involved here as a ‘trialist’

Gittens gets back on the bike

Gittens had a hard 2025-26. His season was essentially a write-off from January, when he picked up a hamstring problem.

Yet he has now scored in three successive friendlies under Alonso – in their behind-closed-doors wins over Crawley and Bromley back in London and here against Western Sydney Wanderers.

We could see the confidence coursing through the left winger. Hopefully for him and Chelsea, this 21-year-old Englishman can remain healthy and enjoy a happier campaign.

Jamie Gittens (right) fires in Chelsea's third goal in Sydney

Wanderers offer stern test

Wanderers finished bottom of the 2025–26 A-League table, so they were not expected to pose many problems to Chelsea, even with so many youngsters involved.

Yet it was possibly helpful for Alonso that the Australian side pressed high throughout. That tested Chelsea’s defenders, and their centre-back pairing of Tosin Adarabioyo, 28, and Josh Acheampong, 20, rarely looked comfortable in possession. Too many passes went straight to the feet of their opponents, who found scoring rather straightforward.

Acheampong was beaten too easily when Wanderers scored their second goal, for example. Aydan Hammond skinned the young central defender before stroking the ball beyond Teddy Sharman-Lowe in goal.

Lots to work on, Austin

Chelsea could do with Austin MacPhee arriving from Aston Villa to become their new set-piece specialist sooner rather than later. Wanderers appeared a threat from dead-ball situations, scoring at one corner which was flicked on from the front and nodded in by Anthony Pantazopoulos at the back.

Sports.title: Milos Kerkez reveals why Andoni Iraola is the 'perfect fit' for Liverpool, how he's stepped up as a leader during pre-season and driving trucks with his dad - aged 10!
Sports.content:
When Milos Kerkez signed for Liverpool last summer, an old colleague from his days in Hungary told Daily Mail Sport he was ‘like a young horse’.

Kicking everybody, a hive of energy unable to sit still, a relentless running – but, as former Hungary No 1 Adam Bogdan added at the time, it was always obvious this eccentric individual would make it to the top.

After spending time with Kerkez in a swanky rooftop bar in Chicago, it was hard not to let that verdict pop back to mind.

In an engaging and at times hilarious chat with the Liverpool left back, Kerkez is here to discuss all things from driving Serbian trucks at age 10, getting a ‘smack’ from his dad when he does not play well and his friendship with UFC fighter Paddy ‘The Baddy’ Pimblett.

But first, Kerkez is the best-placed player to offer insight on the new regime. Having signed from Bournemouth for £40m last summer, the Serbian-born Hungary international knows Andoni Iraola and his backroom staff better than any player at Anfield.

‘I was delighted, honestly,’ says the 22-year-old when asked how he reacted to Iraola’s appointment. ‘I worked for him before and he helped me and improved me a lot in the two years that I spent with him.

Kerkez signed for Liverpool from Bournemouth for £40m last summer - and knows Andoni Iraola and his backroom staff better than any player at Anfield

'If you see footage of how we all are after training – all lying down! – then you can see what he is preparing us for,' Kerkez says of Iraola

‘I was really happy, obviously for myself but also for the team. Everyone knows what type of football he plays, I think he is the perfect fit for us.

‘It’s the intensity. He’s not scared to play one-on-one all over the pitch, to press high and to be on the front foot always. If you see footage of how we all are after training – all lying down! – then you can see what he is preparing us for.

‘He is very professional. He likes to talk sometimes but not a lot. Maybe he doesn’t want to get too close to some players and wants to show that everyone is the same in the team and doesn't want to get too close to anyone in particular. He keeps it professional with a lot of hard work.’

At this point, Kerkez puffs out his cheeks and wipes a bead of sweat from his brow. He has just returned from a training session at the HQ of MLS side, Chicago Fire, where the squad have been put through their paces in the searing Illinois heat.

It is understood the left-back has taken it upon himself to step up as a leader on this pre-season tour noting that senior stars such as Virgil van Dijk and Alisson will not partake in the trip. Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate have all departed the club.

But at heart, Kerkez feels like a kid with the innocence of youth, loving every day living out his dream as a top-level footballer.

It was a journey that started on the streets of Serbia, which he believed left him in good stead to make it, following a similar journey to one of the biggest names in the NBA, Denver Nuggets centre Nikola Jokic, nicknamed ‘The Joker’.

‘I grew up a bit different in Serbia,’ says Kerkez, who says he was bored of the summer holidays after 10 days that he spent in Serbia, Spain and Montenegro. ‘We grew up different. It's just your job, do your own damn job.

‘For example, I started to drive a truck when I was 10 years old. I don't know if it's legal or not! It's just a bit different. We're more on the street. I don't know. I can say 10 other things that I did when I was younger… I won't. I gave you this example!’

It is worth pointing out that Kerkez’s father, Sebastijan, was also present – ‘he was doing the pedals, I was quite small so couldn’t catch them – and the youngster was merely sitting on his lap while steering the big-wheeler down the dirt tracks.

When Kerkez signed for Liverpool last summer, an old colleague from his days in Hungary told Daily Mail Sport he was ‘like a young horse’, a hive of energy unable to sit still

Kerkez Snr lives with his son now alongside mother Tijana and gives him lifts to training most days.

The Kerkezes are a tight-knit family. Brother Marko, 26, plays for Aris in the Greek league, while the eldest of the trio is Rade, who worked in a chemical factory. Rade got married this year, which led to some confusion when Milos posted a picture on Instagram with the bride.

‘Everyone gets this wrong!’ beams the left back when asked if he got married. ‘It was my oldest brother. In Serbia it is normal for the younger brothers to take the bride to the church. That’s what I did and now everyone thinks I got married.

‘I keep having to explain to a lot of people that I never got married. It was my oldest brother, not me. I was going around the club and people started to congratulate me. I’m like, “No, I’m not ready for this yet!” It was not me, it was Rade.’

As for his father, Kerkez adds: ‘Paddy the Baddie! My dad met a friend, who is close with Paddy. Then my Dad met Paddy and I came and I met him. I follow UFC a lot. Nice guy… A Scouser. Crazy!

‘My family are very important. My brothers have their own lives now but my parents are with me and I am much happier they are with me, my mum and dad.

‘He is here to smack me sometimes on the top of the head to remind me! Sometimes you play a few good games and you maybe start to get a bit carried away. But my dad is here to smack me, I come straight back down and I switch straight back on. They are very important.’

Kerkez, as is becoming clear, is different to most footballers and his turn of phrase could set him up for a post-playing career as a stand-up comedian.

There is quite a Hungarian community building in Liverpool. Dominik Szoboszlai captained the Reds in their first pre-season friendly, while a back-up goalkeeper Armin Pecsi is impressing team-mates with his calmness on the ball, though he will be loaned out this term.

Academy sources also rave about teenager Erik Farkas, born in Hungary but is eligible to play for England if he makes it. He has trained with the first team.

At one point last season, Slot joked that he thought Mohamed Salah was Hungarian as he spent so much time with Szoboszlai and Kerkez. The trio were good pals and Kerkez says: ‘We speak often. I don't know who he is signing for! We just talk about vacations.’

Kerkez has learned a lot from him and Robertson and adds: ‘Andy helped me a lot. Like I said many times, he's a legend. He did a lot of big things, won everything. He's someone I look up to. Obviously, I'm here. I want to make my own thing.

‘We all know what Andy (Robertson) did for the club, I'm not running away from that. I want to make my own way. I'm going to work hard. I know what it means to play for Liverpool. I showed it a bit last year and I am going to show it more this year.

‘As for Mo, I saw on the TV before we left the AXA (training centre), how many goals and assists Mo had, it was 300 and something. I just walked out! What is this?!

‘Time flies, a new generation comes with new players and hopefully everything will be good.’

Sports.title: Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Goodwood on Wednesday on ITV
Sports.content:
Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Goodwood on Wednesday on ITV

The in-form tipster hopes to continue his run of winning selections on day two of Glorious Goodwood when he has three tips including Ban Royale in the opener

View Image Steve Jones with his picks for Glorious Goodwood on ITV

Make it pay with Bay on day two of Glorious Goodwood. BAY ROYALE (1.50) has shown heaps of promise in three novice and maiden races. He now makes his handicap debut and he looks to have been handed an attractive weight.

It’s hard to understand how he is priced up at much bigger odds than both Hatteen and Infraad, considering he was much too good for both rivals on his return to action at Nottingham in May.

He couldn’t quite follow up under a penalty when runner-up – again at Nottingham – but he bumped into smart prospect Knights Charge and the front pair were well clear of the rest.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

A two-month break since that run should have done him some good and Harry Eustace’s well-bred three-year-old should enjoy the step up to 1m4f for the first time. Have 1pt each-way at 10-1.

ARDUIS INVICTA (5.00) is fairly unexposed over 6f and this speed-favouring course should play to her strengths. She was placed at Listed level as a juvenile last autumn and she has been holding her form this season.

After finishing runner-up over 5f at Musselburgh, she put in another decent performance, despite finding herself short of room at a crucial stage, when fourth at York last month. She looks capable of going close. Have 1pt each-way at 40-1. A few bookies are paying out on six places.

DEFENCE MINISTER (5.40) hasn’t had much luck with the draw in two starts since making a winning return on Kempton’s all-weather track in March. He had little chance racing out of stall one on the far side in the Victoria Cup at Ascot in May in a race dominated by horses that raced towards the stands’ side.

It was a similar story in the Buckingham Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot when he used up a lot of energy to cross towards the favoured nearside from another unhelpful stall. He didn’t have the greatest draw in the race 12 months ago but it didn’t stop him finishing an excellent fourth in a race where the form worked out really well.

This year’s race doesn’t look as strong and, although the luck of the draw has deserted him once again, it’s not impossible to get a decent early position from his stall 13. If he does finally get the rub of the green, he should be very competitive. Have 1pt each-way at 25-1. Most firms are offering five places.

Sports.title: Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’
Sports.content:
Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’

Trawlerman was practically stopped in his tracks by the riderless Amiloc in the straight before Scandinavia completed an impressive victory in the Group 1

View 2 Images Scandinavia chases the loose Amiloc at Goodwood (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

A loose horse caused chaos in the £500,000 Goodwood Cup after getting in the way ‘in the most important part of the race’ on Tuesday.

‌



The 2m Group 1 was supposed to produce a rematch between Ascot Gold Cup first and second, Scandinavia and Trawlerman, the horse who trains in special goggles to protect his eyes from the sun.

‌



Yet there was drama from the outset as first Trawlerman anticipated the start to burst out of the gate half a length in front of the rest. Then Amiloc lost his rider Hector Crouch who, after a valiant effort to stay in the saddle, was dumped on the turf.

‌



The riderless Amiloc decided to race ahead of the field, with Trawlerman kept a safe distance back leading the rest of the field.

But as soon as William Buick launched his bid for victory, Amiloc came right across the front of him, forcing the jockey to take evasive action to avoid a collision. With momentum lost, Scandinavia forged clear to win by eight and a half lengths.

Describing the interference afterwards, Buick said: “It’s significant. It’s hard to say how significant. He got in the way in the most important part of the race. It definitely had an effect.”

‌



View 2 Images Hector Crouch goes off the side of Amiloc (circled) as Trawlerman (far side) steals an advantage (Image: ITV)

Trainer John Gosden said: “When you’ve been crossed like that and checked, he’s not the type to turn around and start quickening. We got the worst of it and we went from being a length and a half in front to a length and a half behind. That’s racing.”

The stewards report said: “Approximately 2 furlongs out, the riderless AMILOC edged right-handed towards the rail resulting in the rider of TRAWLERMAN (IRE) having to take a check for a number of strides when placed on the heels of AMILOC, but after viewing a recording of the incident, it was found that no riding offence was involved.”

‌



After looking into the incidents at the start the stewards were satisfied that Amiloc was a runner “as the rider was mounted as the start was effected before AMILOC jumped left-handed, resulting in Crouch catching his leg on the starting stalls, causing him to become unbalanced and ultimately unseated shortly after the start.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The report added: “TRAWLERMAN (IRE), drawn 8, anticipated the start and accelerated the gate at the same moment as the start had been effected, thereby enabling the gelding to break quickly. Being satisfied that it was not caused through a faulty action of the starting stalls, no further action was taken.”

Article continues below

Scandinavia’s jockey Ryan Moore said: “He couldn’t have done anymore than what he done today. I never asked him for everything.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory

Anthony Joshua was dropped twice in the opening round by Kristian Prenga on Saturday night, but rallied to a stunning second round knockout in Saudi Arabia

View Image Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

A member of Anthony Joshua's team has brutally hit back at Simon Jordan after the talkSPORT presenter questioned the Brit's knockout victory over Kristian Prenga.

‌



'AJ' returned to the ring on Saturday night for the first time since being involved in a tragic car crash over in Nigeria which resulted in the deaths of close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion was dropped twice in the opening round by the Albanian, but sensationally rallied to a second round knockout victory. Joshua's remarkable win has guaranteed a date with long-time rival Tyson Fury - which is due to take place before the end of the year.

‌



Yet Jordan was rather sceptical of the end result, writing: “Not having that … #anthonyjoshua fight. Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how’s that ? … Prenga totally different in 2nd. Something not quite right , all designed to rinse maximum amount of money …”

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jake Paul and Eddie Hearn team up in shock move to end heated rivalry READ MORE :

Sergey Lapin, Director of Team Usyk, has since brutally hit back at Jordan's remarks. Joshua teamed up with the Ukrainian's team prior to his bout with YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul back in December - and Lapin once again played a key role on Saturday night.

In an interview with Action Network, Lapin said: "What do I think of Simon Jordan’s comments? I suppose they also told Prenga to walk straight into a punch that weighed one and a half tonnes. Everyone is entitled to their own theories. I have a friend who still believes the Earth is flat and that space doesn’t exist. Personally, I’d rather discuss what actually happened inside the ring than someone else’s imagination."

Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss READ MORE :

Lapin was quick to turn his attentions to Joshua versus Fury, and is confident his man can secure a devastating knockout over the 'Gypsy King.' "Time certainly plays a role. It helps you recover, refine your game, and sharpen your timing. But time alone doesn’t win great fights," he said.

Article continues below

"When it comes to Joshua versus Fury, I genuinely believe AJ can knock Tyson Fury out. This is the kind of fight where one mistake changes everything. Both men have what I call a “red button”—one decisive shot capable of ending the night. The question isn’t whether the fight happens in one month or six. The question is who finds that moment first. That’s why I believe AJ can finish the fight inside the distance."

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim admits to Man Utd mistakes and explains how sacking has changed him
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim admits to Man Utd mistakes and explains how sacking has changed him

Manchester United parted company with Ruben Amorim in January, who has since taken on the manager's job at Serie A giants AC Milan

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim has discussed the 'mistakes' he made in charge of Manchester United (Image: Giuseppe Cottini/Getty Images)

Ruben Amorim has opened up about the ‘mistakes’ he made during his time as Manchester United head coach. Amorim spent 15 months in charge at Old Trafford before his departure back in January, and has explained how his exit has changed him as a manager.

‌



United appointed Amorim as their new head coach in October 2024 following the departure of Erik ten Hag, before going on to be replaced by Michael Carrick at the turn of the year. Since leaving United, Amorim has been named as the new manager of AC Milan and is currently gearing up for the start of the new Serie A season.

‌



Amorim has now spoken about his time at United and what he has learned from his spell at Old Trafford, admitting that he made “a lot of mistakes” during his time with the Red Devils.

‌



When quizzed about what went wrong during his time as United boss, Amorim said in an interview with Sky Italy: “The first thing is that it doesn’t matter anymore. That is the feeling.

Lisandro Martinez reveals why Argentina turned backs on Spain players lifting World Cup READ MORE :

Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks READ MORE :

“There’s a history, then something happens, the context changes, and you focus on the next challenge. I learned a lot.

“It would be hard to point to one thing. But the important thing that I clearly know is that I made a lot of mistakes.

‌



“When you do this kind of reflection, and you understand that it was not just their fault, but also my fault, I think you can be a better coach and a better man.”

Amorim won 25 of his 63 matches in charge at United, suffering 23 defeats along the way, too. The 41-year-old has also spoke about the reasons why he decided to take the job at Milan, as well as sending another message to United.

He said: “I was really honoured to be the manager of Man United at the time, but now I’m at Milan. I spoke with some people at the club, like Massaro and Baresi; we exchanged messages.

‌



View 2 Images AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim (Image: Claudio Villa/AC Milan via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“That is the most important thing. To understand what kind of club I am and what the history of the club is.

‌



“For me, it was easier this time, because I’ve been a Milan fan since I was a boy. I understand the culture of the club and their history. But that is the past.

“Our goal is to be the new future. They chose me for a reason, and one of the reasons is that I like to look at teams that are struggling. I know it’s tough, but we want to rebuild something.

“We have many things in a good place. The staff is in a good place; the organisation is fantastic. If this is my final destination, I’ll be pleased because it’s a dream to coach this club.”

Sports.title: Kaiya Fraser shows ‘balls of steel’ to ride biggest winner of career at Glorious Goodwood
Sports.content:
Kaiya Fraser shows ‘balls of steel’ to ride biggest winner of career at Glorious Goodwood

Punters were raving about the 23-year-old from Hackney who, riding at Group level for the first time, landed the Vintage Stakes on Dr Rascal

View 2 Images Kaiya Fraser: rode Dr Rascal to victory in the Vintage Stakes (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

Kaiya Fraser showed ‘balls of steel’ to ride the biggest winner of his short career at Glorious Goodwood on Tuesday.

‌



The 23-year-old from Hackney in east London was riding for the first time at Group 1 level on the Oliver Cole-trained Dr Rascal in the Group 2 Coral Vintage Stages. Just 17 days earlier Fraser was dragged off Dr Rascal when a rival runner attacked him and bit him on the thigh before a race at Ascot, only for the unflappable young jockey to remount and win the race.

‌



The unbeaten colt was facing better fancied horses representing Godolphin and Aidan O’Brien’s Ballydoyle outfit.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

On a tricky track like Goodwood, Fraser’s lack of top race experience could have cost him. However he tracked Amo Racing’s Pikachu then went for a narrow gap along the far rail that looked like it was closing rapidly.

Yet Dr Rascal forced his way through and picked up again to win by half a length from O’Brien’s Haffner with 5-4 favourite Al Hudaiba third.

Punters on social media were full of praise for the jockey. “Absolute balls of steel on Kaiya Fraser there,” said one.

‌



Sky Sports Racing presenter Dave Orton said: ‘What a rascal! That took some balls, no way the horse would’ve got out, with Ryan Moore on his outer, had he waited there. Take a bow Kaiya Fraser.”

View 2 Images Dr Rascal (far side) beat Haffner and Al Hudaiba at Goodwood (Image: Getty Images)

Fraser was called to a stewards’ inquiry straight after the race but the officials ruled he had gone for “a tight but legitimate gap” and no riding offence was involved. He was cautioned for allowing Dr Rascal and drift left near the line.

‌



The jockey said: “First of all I want to thank my Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ without whom this would not be possible.

“I want to thank all the owners and Mr Cole for putting me on and trusting me. This is a great day, I’m very happy and happy to get the job done for them.

“This means everything. This is what we wake up for every morning. I’ve put so much hard work to get to where I am today. I am very thankful for all the people who’ve helped me.

Sports.title: Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves
Sports.content:
Chelsea have raised eyebrows in the market by going after Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso throws a curveball with his recruitment plans.

The Blues have been associated with some of the most blockbuster transfers of the last five years, landing the likes of Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo and Morgan Rogers for huge sums.

Rogers is their big capture of the summer, but as Alonso looks to put his stamp on a squad that floundered last season, finishing 10th, he's turned to some tried and tested Premier League performers who are certainly closing in on the ends of their careers.

Welbeck, now 35, is enjoying an Indian summer to his career and was seen as an outsider for England's World Cup squad. He's not played for a major side since leaving Arsenal in 2019, but could find his way back via Stamford Bridge.

‌



Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing READ MORE :

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Not long after it emerged that Chelsea were working on a deal to land Jordan Henderson, another veteran performer at 36. The midfielder spent last year at Brentford after playing for in Saudi Arabia and the Netherlands, but clearly Alonso and Thomas Tuchel see something in him with the ex-Liverpool man part of the World Cup squad.

While such moves have been ridiculed they have more than worked in the past. Players are playing later and later now, without their level dropping. Just because its not a long-term investment, doesn't mean it can't work for the here and now.

Chelsea have ultimately underdelivered with their plan to continue investing in youth, which has got them nowhere for all the talk of potential and having the youngest squad in the league. Ultimately they need players who can get the job done.

View 4 Images Danny Welbeck could get one last big move to a top club (Image: GLYN KIRK, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



After all Henderson is a man who has lifted the Premier League and the Champions League during his career. Here are some cases of veteran moves that more than paid off for their club.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic to Man Utd

The Swede was a free agent after leaving PSG and decided to team back up with Jose Mourinho, who he'd worked with successfully at Inter Milan. Ibrahimovic was well into his 30s but had scored at an alarming rate whilst in Paris and decided to show he could crack it in England. He scored on debut and whilst the Red Devils didn't have their finest campaign Ibrahimovic didn't let his level drop. He finished with 28 goals - 17 more than his closest team-mate. He would also come up trumps, scoring the winner to claim the Community Shield and the Carabao Cup.

View 4 Images Zlatan Ibrahimovic claimed three trophies in his year at Man Utd

Gary McAllister to Liverpool

Then Reds boss Gerard Houllier was questioned when he signed a 35-year-old McAllister on a free after he'd left Coventry, especially when he had a young Steven Gerrard coming through the ranks. However he would prove a stroke of genius as Liverpool won their treble of trophies. His experience more than told and the Scotland midfielder was man of the match in the 2001 UEFA Cup final win over Alaves, scored a penalty winner against Barcelona in the semi-final before that and came up with an iconic 44-yard free-kick that won the Merseyside derby in stoppage time.

‌



Esteban Cambiasso to Leicester

He was 34 when he decided to call time on a decade at Inter, where he'd won five Serie A titles, four Coppa Italia crown and and a Champions League. The Argentine swapped that for newly promoted Leicester and would inspire late season form that kept them in the Premier League.

View 4 Images Esteban Cambiasso helped keep Leicester in the top flight (Image: Getty Images)

His first meaningful contribution saw him score in a comeback 5-3 win over the Red Devils. He was named Foxes Player of the Year after his impressive spell but chose not to sign a new deal with Leicester securing their historic title success the following year.

Jurgen Klinsmann to Tottenham

The German was by no means adored in England when he first rocked up at Tottenham in 1994 from Monaco. Klinsmann scored on his debut against Sheffield Wednesday and immediately won over supporters with a diving celebration, having been accused of the act previously. Klinsmann scored an amazing 30 goals in all competitions in his only season with Tottenham in his first spell. The forward then returned to Spurs at the age of 33 with Klinsmann’s goals saving the club from relegation after arriving in the winter.

‌



Claude Makelele to Chelsea

Maybe not in the peak veteran category having been 30 when he moved from Real Madrid, but their struggles after his exit showcased just how influential he was. The Blues flourished with the Frenchman at the base of their midfield and he effectively had a role and his position named after him, he was that good at it. He helped Chelsea win two Premier League titles during their first period under Jose Mourinho.

Sports.title: Darren Till explains Yoel Romero U-turn ahead of bare-knuckle fight
Sports.content:
Darren Till explains Yoel Romero U-turn ahead of bare-knuckle fight

The former UFC welterweight challenger will take on ex-UFC star Yoel Romero in a bare-knuckle boxing contest in Manchester later this year

View Image Darren Till will take on Yoel Romero in bare-knuckle boxing clash later this year (Image: Getty Images)

Darren Till admits getting over his years of 'trauma' and 'nightmares' of Yoel Romero eventually led to him performing a stunning U-turn.

‌



Till and Romero will meet in a bare-knuckle boxing showdown at BKFC 94 on September 26 - which is scheduled to take place at the AO Arena in Manchester.

‌



After parting ways with Misfits Boxing earlier this year, the former UFC welterweight title challenger made the decision to jump over to BKFC and try his hand at fighting without gloves. In May, he was made to show some real adversity on his promotional debut after being dropped in the opening round by Aaron Chalmers, but the Scouse scrapper would go on to secure a brutal knockout.

‌



In his second appearance, he faces a major step up in competition in the shape of 49-year-old Romero. At one point, the pair competed in the same division in the UFC. Just days after beating Kelvin Gastelum on his 185lb debut, Till sensationally called for a fight with Romero - but backtracked after admitting he was 'drunk' when he sent a warning to the Cuban behemoth.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jake Paul and Eddie Hearn team up in shock move to end heated rivalry READ MORE :

Worrying Anthony Joshua footage emerges from dramatic KO win READ MORE :

Every time Till has been asked if he is serious about being afraid of Romero, the Liverpudlian suggested it's a tongue-in-cheek ploy. “Of course, mate, he’s a beast - I’m terrified,” he said in 2020. But six years on, he seems to have changed his mind and will now finally settle the score with the MMA veteran.

Explaining his U-turn, Till said: “I’ve finally got over my years of trauma & nightmares of Yoel Romero. So, let’s f***** do this!!” While Romero added: “He’s been running his mouth for too long, on September 26 I’m going to close it permanently in Manchester."

Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss READ MORE :

The pair will meet in a catchweight of 190 pounds, and after the bout was confirmed, BKFC supremo David Feldman said: “This is the biggest event we’ve promoted in the United Kingdom between two international combat sport superstars. Both Darren and Yoel have been very successful in their BKFC fights and both are looking for the biggest challenge in the promotion.

Article continues below

"It’s a very heated rivalry and no question, this will be bombs away from the opening bell. It’s truly a can’t miss combat sporting event in the United Kingdom and I strongly encourage fans to purchase early for September 26. We’ll be announcing a tremendous undercard featuring the baddest bare-knuckle fighters in the United Kingdom shortly.”

September's showdown with Romero will mark Till's second contest in his three-fight deal with BKFC, but Feldman confirms he is set to hold talks with the Scouser's management team in a bid to extend the fighter's current deal. There had been whispers of a potential clash between Till and rival Mike Perry, but the BKFC president stated that they're looking to stage the fight next February. Perry recently confirmed his return to action, and will take on Dillon Danis on August 29 inside the Octagon.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola 'reaches verbal agreement' with Liverpool as blockbuster transfer advances
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola 'reaches verbal agreement' with Liverpool as blockbuster transfer advances

Liverpool have made Bradley Barcola a top target and Reds manager Andoni Iraola spoken to the Paris Saint-Germain star, who's been valued at a jaw-dropping £145million

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is keen to join Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Bradley Barcola has reached an agreement in principle to join Liverpool after holding positive talks with Andoni Iraola. The Reds boss recently confirmed their plans to sign a winger and Barcola, 23, is a top target.

‌



The Frenchman be allowed to leave Paris Saint-Germain this summer for the right price. It's been reported that PSG will demand a staggering £145million for his signature.

‌



Now L'Equipe claim that Barcola has given his approval to the big-money move. However, Liverpool and PSG are still far away in their respective valuations of the ex-Lyon star.

‌



It comes after Premier League rivals Arsenal decided against pursuing Barcola. The Gunners are instead prioritising a stunning move for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool's Milos Kerkez explains why he chose to keep distance from Andy Robertson READ MORE :

Barcola has helped the French club win back-to-back Champions Leagues. Since joining PSG for around £38m in 2023, the winger has scored 39 goals and provided 35 assists in 152 appearances.

‌



During the World Cup, where he was in and out of France's starting XI, he revealed that he was uncertain about his future at club level. "I'm focused on the World Cup," Barcola said. "What happens after that, I don't know."

Meanwhile, Iraola told a press conference last week that Liverpool 'definitely need to sign a winger'. "When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," the Reds boss explained.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
