World.title: New ambassador to the US: I'm ready to run in presidential elections
World.content:
Incoming Estonian ambassador to the United States Hannes Hanso has said he would be willing to be a candidate at September's Estonian presidential elections, if asked.

Hanso, 54, until recently Estonia's ambassador to China, said he would make a good president if elected, adding more than one party has floated the idea.

"It is true that two or three parties have discussed my possible candidacy in various formats. Also in a broader circle. That is, in itself, a great honor for me," the newly appointed representative to Washington, told Vikerraadio's Uudis+ program Tuesday.

In response to the host's question about what his response would be if party leaders asked him to run for president, Hanso said: "What would I say? It would be tough for us to reorganize our family life once again, but I would definitely be ready. I have no doubt that I would be a good president of the republic."

Hanso noted his resume includes a stint as minister of defense (2015-2016). He has also served in local government, including as a mayor, and on local councils as well, and national politics as a past Riigikogu member, where he chaired the Riigikogu's foreign affairs and national defense committees at various times. He was also briefly an MEP (2019).

"If those are the experiences and competencies that are being sought, then as a citizen it would almost be irresponsible to say 'no,' if such a consensus could be built around me. To refuse to take on that responsibility. Then we would have to reshuffle our cards once again, and the children would also be very happy that they could finally live in Estonia again. In short, Hannes Hanso would not throw in the towel and would say 'yes'."

Hanso also said he does not like the situation which has emerged around Estonia's presidential election process and the upcoming election in particular.

Ballots being counted at the first round of the 2021 presidential election. Source: Erik Peinar, Chancellery of the Riigikogu

"The world is unstable and turbulent. We need some clarity, and people should be honest. If they have an ambition to become president, they should say so. Be a man and say it, or be a woman and say it: 'Yes, I am interested. I believe we all have a responsibility for these matters.' Standing behind a bush, hedging, or keeping the door open without saying anything – there is really no need for such fear. It is the greatest honor a person can have: to be the head of state, the country's leader."

Hanso was appointed Estonia's next ambassador to the U.S. in early June, replacing Kristjan Prikk, who is to become Estonia's ambassador to NATO later in the year. Hanso had been ambassador to Beijing up to his new appointment.

Hanso's declaration comes at a time when several other public figures have either been put forward by politicians as candidates, or declared their own interest in running. The first group includes Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, while former Defense League commander Riho Ühtegi is in the latter camp.

Estonia's presidents are elected by the Riigikogu in the first instance, with a majority of 68 at the 101-seat chamber needed, meaning cross-party support of coalition and opposition parties is required for a candidate to get voted in.

If three rounds of voting draw a blank, the process moves to the regional electoral college.

Nominations open for candidates on August 21, and close August 24. The Riigikogu voting rounds start on September 2.

Hanso was a member of the Social Democratic Party (SDE) from February 2009 until June 2019.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 526,000 bpd in May and June
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s average oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 526,470 barrels per day, compared to about 329,500 barrels per day in April, amid ongoing shipping and energy disruptions in the Gulf region.

The revenues generated from Iraqi oil exports saw an improvement over the last two months, supported by a relative increase in shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and the activation of alternative export routes.

Oil prices fluctuated, remaining high at around $100 per barrel during May before falling below that level in June.

The rising oil prices boosted Iraq’s export income in May and June 2026, when there were fears about supply constraints and increased Asian demand, notably from China and India.

Iraqi oil exports have been under growing strain since the beginning of March, following the suspension of loading operations at southern ports due to the US war against Iran, which had a direct impact on marine security in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO), Iraq’s total oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 32.11 million barrels, with a monthly average of over 16 million barrels.

The country’s oil exports reached 9.88 million barrels in April and around 18.6 million barrels in March.

Iraqi oil export earnings in May and June 2026 reached approximately $2.33 billion, averaging $1.16 billion per month, compared to $1.87 billion in April, $1.95 billion in March, and approximately $6.81 billion in February.

Experts believe that the current price levels of oil are likely to provide Baghdad with a better financial margin to mitigate some losses incurred from the significant decline in exports, even amidst ongoing security tensions in the region.

World.title: Iraqi PM arrives in Turkey on an official visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on Tuesday, for an official visit following an invitation from President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that his trip to Turkey will focus on investments, water, and development projects, as well as efforts to enhance stability in the region.

Turkish media highlighted the significance of the visit, as it is expected to broaden constructive collaboration between the two countries, particularly in the areas of water, energy, security, and economic cooperation, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

In addition to trade, security cooperation, and combating terrorism, al-Zaidi will discuss establishing a cooperative water management entity based on shared interests, as well as scientific collaboration and investment in advanced technology, to serve the interests of both Iraq and Turkey.

Al-Zaidi is scheduled to fly to Saudi Arabia on Thursday for an official visit, following his diplomatic trip to the Turkish capital, Ankara.

The trip is part of a larger regional diplomatic tour aiming to maintain regional balance and strengthen Iraq’s business connections.

The prime minister recently conducted high-level diplomatic visits to the United States on July 13 and Iran on July 23.

World.title: Ukraine rejects Iraqi official’s claims of Ukrainian cell operating in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday dismissed statements by Iraq’s National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi, who claimed that Iraqi authorities had arrested a Ukrainian-linked cell responsible for carrying out attacks inside the country.

In an official statement, the ministry said the allegations were “groundless” and noted that no evidence had been presented to support the claims. It also pointed out that Al-Aboudi himself acknowledged during a televised interview that investigations into the matter were still ongoing.

According to the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry, Iraqi authorities did not communicate any information or concerns through diplomatic channels before the allegations were made publicly.

The ministry said that if Iraqi officials possessed credible evidence, the issue should have been raised through official diplomatic mechanisms rather than announced during a television interview. Instead, Kyiv said it first learned of the accusations through media reports.

Furthermore, Ukraine described the public remarks by a senior Iraqi official as “unacceptable and irresponsible” in the absence of supporting evidence. The ministry stressed that such statements contradict the principles of mutual respect between friendly nations and risk undermining relations between Iraq and Ukraine.

At the same time, Kyiv reaffirmed that it considers Iraq an important partner in the Middle East and remains committed to strengthening political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation between the two countries.

The Foreign Ministry also argued that the allegations mirror Russian propaganda narratives aimed at damaging Ukraine’s international reputation and weakening its partnerships across the Middle East.

Additionally, the statement suggested that the incident could have resulted from external information influence or formed part of a coordinated information campaign intended to disrupt Iraqi-Ukrainian relations.

Ukraine called on Iraqi authorities to address what it described as unfounded allegations and to prevent state institutions from promoting misinformation that could serve the interests of third parties.

The Ukrainian response follows remarks made on Monday by National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi during an interview on Dijlah TV. Al-Aboudi said Iraqi intelligence had identified what he described as Ukrainian interference inside Iraq and claimed security forces had arrested several individuals who allegedly carried out attacks on Iraqi territory.

He further stated that those detained confessed during questioning to working on behalf of Ukraine. However, Al-Aboudi did not identify the facilities allegedly targeted or specify whether the alleged operations extended beyond Iraq’s borders.

He also acknowledged that investigations into attacks carried out inside Iraq remain complex and require further examination before responsibility can be definitively assigned.

World.title: Iraqi PM expands powers as political deadlock delays cabinet completion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A dispute over Iraq’s remaining vacant cabinet positions has expanded beyond the selection of ministers, with political factions now focusing on the growing authority of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, according to a report published by Al-Mada newspaper.

The debate follows the leak of an official document indicating that Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi has reactivated and expanded the powers of the Commander-in-Chief Office, placing several key security institutions under its supervision while the Ministries of Interior and Defense remain without permanent ministers.

According to Al-Mada, several political sources believe the expanded office significantly increases the prime minister’s direct oversight of Iraq’s security apparatus.

The report says the office now oversees the Ministries of Interior and Defense, the Counter-Terrorism Service, the National Intelligence Service, the National Security Service, the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), border crossings, military industries, and other security-related institutions.

Consequently, some political figures have described the move as a “quiet coup” against Iraq’s post-2003 political framework, arguing that it centralizes authority within the prime minister’s office while reducing the practical influence of future ministers.

Meanwhile, Iraq’s cabinet remains incomplete, with only 14 ministries currently filled while nine ministerial portfolios remain vacant. According to the report, political negotiations have become increasingly complicated, as disagreements now extend beyond candidate names to broader questions of political influence and institutional control.

Sources cited by Al-Mada said the State of Law Coalition has proposed rotating senior security positions as part of efforts to break the deadlock, particularly regarding the Interior Ministry, which traditionally falls under the Shiite political share, while the Defense Ministry is typically allocated to Sunni representatives.

However, negotiations have yet to produce a breakthrough.

At the same time, Al-Mada reported that U.S. objections have become one of the main obstacles preventing completion of the cabinet. Political sources quoted in the report claim Washington opposes appointing individuals affiliated with armed factions to ministerial positions or senior executive offices.

The report says these objections have complicated negotiations among members of the Coordination Framework, with some factions insisting that if their nominees are rejected, similar restrictions should apply to other political parties. As a result, discussions over the remaining cabinet positions have largely stalled.

Political analysts interviewed by Al-Mada argue that the continued delay in appointing ministers has allowed Prime Minister Al-Zaidi greater flexibility in managing state institutions through acting officials and appointments within his office.

According to the report, some political parties fear that prolonging the vacancies could further strengthen the prime minister’s influence over Iraq’s security establishment, making future ministerial appointments less significant.

The report also notes that recent anti-corruption campaigns and shifting political alliances have altered the balance of power within the Coordination Framework, adding another layer of complexity to negotiations.

Supporters of the government, however, argue that the current arrangements are necessary to maintain continuity while negotiations continue.

Officials quoted by Al-Mada said acting appointments and the reactivation of the Commander-in-Chief Office ensure that security institutions continue functioning despite the absence of permanent ministers.

They also expressed confidence that political forces will eventually reach an agreement to complete the cabinet, stressing that Iraq faces significant challenges, including anti-corruption efforts, security reforms, weapons control, and economic pressures linked to oil exports.

Nevertheless, the report suggests that political parties continue to use the vacant ministries as leverage in negotiations with the prime minister, making the timeline for completing the government uncertain.

World.title: US drone shot down in western Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An unknown drone, first claimed by Iranian official media IRIB as a US surveillance one, crashed within a residential complex near the Haditha Dam in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

Iraqi police and security agencies later indicated that the drone’s origin remains unknown, according to Al-Jazeera.

The debris was discovered blazing in a residential compound near the Haditha Dam in Anbar.

Local police stated that there were no recorded injuries or civilian deaths as a result of the collision.

Iranian state media swiftly released images of the smoking debris, claiming it was a US drone shot down amid broader regional activity.

The incident took place during a night of broad military conflict in Iraq, which included many drone attacks and defensive responses.

At least four Iranian drones attacked targets northeast of the capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, Erbil, sparking a huge defensive reaction, including over ten US jets and drones sent to inspect the skies.

Air defense systems were activated at Anbar’s Ain al-Asad Air Base in response to a drone strike.

Explosions, alleged suicide drones, and radar interruptions were also reported at Camp Taji, Balad Air Base, and Imam Ali Base in southern Iraq.

The US military has not publicly verified the loss of any aircraft in Anbar. Investigations into the model and operator of the crashed drone are still underway.

World.title: Al Zaidi: Iraq and Turkey can build a regional success story through economic integration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi said on Tuesday that the Middle East needs new success stories built on economic integration rather than conflict, arguing that Iraq and Turkey have the potential to create a model regional partnership through joint investment, infrastructure, and trade.

The remarks came in an article published by Turkey’s Anadolu Agency ahead of Al Zaidi’s official visit to Ankara, where he is expected to meet Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and senior officials.

Al Zaidi said relations between Iraq and Turkey have traditionally focused on managing issues such as security, water resources, trade, and border crossings. However, he argued that regional changes require a more ambitious vision centered on economic cooperation.

He said Iraq has chosen a path of stability, reform, and development, prioritizing a stronger economy, an effective state, and balanced foreign relations that make regional cooperation a pillar of growth.

According to Al Zaidi, Turkey’s industrial base, strategic location, and expertise in infrastructure, energy, and transportation complement Iraq’s geographic position, creating an opportunity to establish one of the region’s most significant economic partnerships.

The prime minister highlighted the Development Road Project, describing it as more than an Iraqi initiative. He said the corridor could redefine economic connectivity in the Middle East by linking Gulf ports with Asian and European markets.

He added that the project would not only reduce shipping times but also create new cities, industrial zones, investment opportunities, and thousands of jobs, while establishing a new economic artery connecting ports to global markets.

Al Zaidi also stressed that security cooperation remains essential, saying Iraq’s and Turkey’s security are closely linked and require mutual respect for sovereignty as well as joint efforts to combat terrorism and organized crime.

On water issues, he said water is no longer simply a technical matter but a development challenge affecting millions of people. He called for a shared approach based on mutual interests, scientific cooperation, and investment in modern technologies to strengthen water and food security.

“The Middle East needs new success stories,” Al Zaidi wrote, adding that Iraq and Turkey can provide one if they move beyond traditional cooperation toward genuine economic integration.

He said every joint investment, factory, transport route, and energy project represents an investment in regional stability, arguing that lasting stability is built through shared projects rather than conflict.

Later on Tuesday, Al Zaidi departed for Ankara at the head of a high-level government delegation. According to the Prime Minister’s Office, the visit will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation in the fields of economy, water, security, investment, and regional affairs.

The two sides are also expected to review the implementation of existing agreements and memoranda of understanding, while discussing progress on joint infrastructure projects, including the Development Road initiative.

World.title: Drone attack targets Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Drone attacks targeted the Khor Mor gas field in the northern Iraqi province of Sulaymaniyah in the early hours of Tuesday.

The attack on the field, which is Iraq’s largest gas field with reserves estimated at 8.2 trillion cubic feet, was part of a coordinated wave of suspected Iranian drone attacks against the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

Iranian official media reported an attack on the gas field, which is operated by the UAE-based Pearl Consortium that includes Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum.

The gas field supplies the majority of the electricity in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to reports, the strikes were carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which targets Iranian Kurdish resistance groups and US interests in the region.

A few days ago, Iraqi Kurdistan’s Prime Minister Masoud Barzani stated that repeated security threats and drone attacks had caused energy companies to cut domestic output, seriously affecting the region’s electrical infrastructure.

The escalation takes place amid significant geopolitical challenges. On Monday, US President Donald Trump said he was ready to resume military action against Iran if diplomatic efforts to reach a nuclear deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz failed.

Trump stated that he has temporarily stopped military strikes against Iran to give negotiations a chance to work.

World.title: Iraq, Australia cooperate to sentence alleged drug trafficker to life imprisonment
World.content:
An Iraqi court has sentenced convicted drug trafficker Kazem Hamad to life imprisonment after finding him guilty of drug trafficking and links to transnational organized crime, in a case that involved close cooperation between Iraqi and Australian authorities.

The ruling marks a significant development in Iraq’s ongoing campaign against organized crime and narcotics trafficking.

In a statement issued on Monday, Iraq’s judiciary described Hamad as “one of the most wanted individuals by Iraqi and international courts.” According to the judiciary, Hamad was responsible for smuggling large quantities of heroin into both Iraq and Australia.

The statement also accused him of involvement with transnational criminal networks engaged in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, kidnapping, extortion, and organized violence.

Australian authorities have identified Hamad as a key figure in Melbourne’s so-called “tobacco wars,” a violent conflict between organized crime groups competing for control of the illicit tobacco and vape market.

The turf war has been linked to more than 200 arson attacks, firebombings, and extortion incidents across the Australian city. Hamad was deported from Australia in 2023 and was arrested in Iraq in January 2026, where prosecutors charged him with smuggling narcotics into both countries.

The Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed earlier this year that it had provided operational information to support Iraq’s investigation. AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett said in February that the agency would continue cooperating with Iraqi authorities while pursuing its own investigation into Hamad and his alleged criminal network under Operation Carmen.

Australian investigators have also linked Hamad to several serious crimes, including allegations that he played a role in the December 2024 firebombing of Melbourne’s Adass Israel Synagogue, according to Australian media reports.

The life sentence comes as Iraq continues to intensify its fight against drug trafficking and organized crime. Despite imposing some of the region’s toughest penalties, including life imprisonment and the death penalty for major narcotics offenses, Iraq has experienced a sharp rise in drug trafficking and addiction since 2003.

Officials say authorities have arrested thousands of suspects in recent years as part of nationwide anti-drug operations. Iraq was recently ranked third globally in combating narcotics at the World Police Summit in the United Arab Emirates, reflecting the country’s expanding efforts to dismantle trafficking networks.

World.title: 13 Indians stranded aboard vessel in Ukraine amid repeated drone, missile attacks: Report
World.content:
13 Indian seafarers trapped in vessel in Ukraine amid repeated drone, missile attacks

NEW DELHI: Thirteen Indian seafarers are among 15 crew members stranded on board a cargo vessel at Ukraine's Chornomorsk port, where repeated drone and missile attacks have placed the crew in what has been described as a "life-threatening situation", according to the Forward Seamen's Union of India (FSUI).In an urgent appeal posted on X, the union said the vessel, MV AMIR1, remains docked at Chornomorsk while hostilities continue in the surrounding area."MV AMIR1, currently at Ukrainian port Chornomorsk with 15 crew on board, including 13 Indian seafarers, is trapped in a terrible and life-threatening situation," it said.The union alleged that drone and missile attacks were being carried out in the immediate vicinity of the ship, leaving the crew in constant fear."Repeated drone and missile attacks are being attempted in the immediate vicinity of the vessel. The crew is living under constant fear of a direct hit at any moment," it said.The FSUI urged the shipowners, the vessel's flag state, the relevant authorities and the government to intervene immediately to ensure the crew's safety and facilitate their evacuation."We urgently appeal to all concerned authorities, shipowners, flag state, and the Government of India to immediately secure their safety and arrange prompt repatriation," the union said.Calling for urgent action, it added, "Indian seafarers must not be left as sitting targets in conflict zones. Act now."This comes a day after MEA raised concerns with Ukraine over the safety of Indian seafarers in the Black Sea. On Monday, the MEA summoned Ukraine's ambassador to India, Dr Oleksandr Polishchuk, following an attack on the merchant vessel MV OMORFI near the Ukrainian port of Odesa that had four Indian crew members on board.The MEA said the strike resulted in the death of an Indian national and condemned attacks on commercial shipping in the "strongest terms", calling them a threat to maritime safety, freedom of navigation and international commerce. It also urged Kyiv to ensure that commercial vessels carrying civilian seafarers are not targeted.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami distributes subsidies to boost clean mobility; flags off 11 clean fuel vehicles
World.content:
Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday distributed capital grant and incentive subsidy cheques to six primary beneficiary vehicle owners under the Uttarakhand Clean Mobility Transition Policy-2024 at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan, Chief Minister's Camp Office.

The transport department has also completed the subsidy approval process for five additional beneficiaries.

On the occasion, the CM flagged off 11 clean fuel-based vehicles. Addressing the programme, he said that the assistance was not merely financial support but a symbol of the state government's commitment to building a clean, modern, and environmentally sustainable transport system in Uttarakhand. He said the initiative would promote clean fuel-based public transport in urban areas, reduce pollution caused by diesel-powered vehicles, and strengthen environmental conservation efforts.

Dhami said the world is facing the serious challenge of climate change, making it essential to strike a balance between development and environmental protection. He emphasised that development is meaningful only when it remains in harmony with nature and ensures a safe and clean future for coming generations. The CM said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is emerging as a global leader in green energy and sustainable development.





He highlighted initiatives such as the country's target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070, the Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) campaign, the PM e-Bus Sewa scheme, and the expansion of solar and other renewable energy sources as evidence of India's commitment to environmental protection.

Dhami said Uttarakhand, nestled in the Himalayas and revered as Devbhoomi, is the origin of life-giving rivers such as the Ganga and Yamuna.

He noted that the state's rich biodiversity, forests, rivers, and mountain ecosystems are invaluable national assets. Protecting the environment and maintaining ecological balance, he said, is a shared responsibility, adding that the state government's vision is to ensure that development and environmental conservation go hand in hand.The chief minister said that with this vision, the government has implemented the Uttarakhand Clean Mobility Transition Policy-2024.

The policy aims to modernise public transport in urban areas, reduce pollution caused by ageing diesel vehicles, and encourage the adoption of CNG and other clean fuel-based transport systems. He expressed confidence that the policy would lay a strong foundation for a cleaner, safer, and more sustainable transport network across the state. Dhami further said that the state government is continuously expanding the operation of electric buses in Dehradun, Haridwar, and Haldwani.

EV charging stations are also being established across Uttarakhand to provide the necessary infrastructure for clean mobility. He added that work is progressing rapidly on ropeway projects and modern urban transport systems, which will improve traffic management, reduce congestion and pollution in hilly regions, and make transportation safer and more environmentally friendly.

World.title: Delhi Police officer denies authorising alleged RAF pellet gun firing during CJP march: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A senior

officer has denied being present at the spot when a Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel allegedly fired from a pellet gun at protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) Parliament march on July 20, officials said on Tuesday.

A General Diary (GD) entry recorded by the Rapid Action Force (RAF) at Parliament Street police station mentions that the officer was present in Zone-1 near Jantar Mantar when the alleged incident took place, PTI reported.

The officer, however, claimed that he was nearly half a kilometre away from the spot when the pellet rounds were reportedly fired.

Meanwhile, a high-level meeting was held at the Delhi Police headquarters on Tuesday to discuss the GD entry related to the alleged use of non-lethal munitions, including plastic pellets, by the RAF, the specialised riot-control wing of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF).

Attended by senior Delhi Police officers, the meeting focused on the circumstances surrounding the GD entry recorded on July 22 at 1:24 pm.

According to official police records, the GD entry was made ased on information provided by a Deputy Commandant-rank RAF officer. It states that RAF personnel deployed in Zone-1 alongside a Deputy Commissioner of Police-rank Delhi Police officer fired multiple non-lethal munitions after received rmission from the senior police officer.





According to the entry, the RAF fired 55 non-electrical shells, 15 electrical shells, five tear smoke grenades, two rounds from anti-riot guns and two rounds of plastic pellets while controlling the crowd.

Officials said one round of plastic pellets contains four plastic projectiles, which differ from metal pellets and are designed to cause less serious injuries.

The alleged use of plastic pellets has become a major political flashpoint after reports that some protesters sustained grievous pellet injuries during the violence.

Multiple Delhi Police, RAF and CRPF personnel were also injured in the clashes.

Delhi Police has maintained that allegations of the force using pellet guns against protesters are "false and misleading", reiterating its position in a statement on its official X handle. According to the police, more than 65 protesters and over 200 police personnel were injured during the clashes.

World.title: 'Uninformed, unacceptable': CJP claims SC order contradicts govt assurance; warns of protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (

) has threatened to restart its nationwide agitation if the government fails to withdraw FIRs against student protesters, saying a Supreme Court interim order on the batch of PILs related to the protest "rings alarm bells across the country.

"

In an urgent statement posted on X, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said Direction No. 4 of the order is a "direct contradiction" to the government's solemn assurance of July 25 that FIRs would be withdrawn and protesters would not be targeted. The Direction permits governments to proceed with existing FIRs and carry out investigations.

"It was on the strength of that solemn assurance, and in complete good faith, that the Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protest," Das said.

The CJP spokesperson expressed apprehension that the government and BJP-ruled states may "weaponise" the order passed by the bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to continue FIRs against individual protesters and subject them to harassment. "This was precisely our concern from day one: that courts could be used, directly or indirectly, to achieve political ends by targeting peaceful dissent," he said.





Das also pointed to the fact that the interim order was not opposed by the government's lawyers, despite the Centre being fully aware that talks with the CJP had continued until late Monday night and that a "solemn agreement" had already been arrived at on July 25. "The court's uninformed order is therefore wholly unacceptable," he said.

"A solemn public assurance given to thousands of young students and protesters cannot be diluted, undermined, or rendered meaningless through subsequent legal developments, in a surreptitious manner.

It only results in breach of public trust," Das added.

He clarified that nothing in the interim order prevents the government or BJP/NDA-ruled states from withdrawing FIRs or deciding not to proceed against peaceful protesters, as done by Bihar and Assam governments. "The power to withdraw or not pursue such cases continues to rest with the executive. The court has not mandated that governments must definitely continue with the FIRs.

That would be a deliberate misreading," he said.

Das demanded that the government immediately place the terms of the July 25 assurance before the Supreme Court "so that there is complete transparency regarding the commitments already made to the youth of this country."

"The youth of India entered into this understanding in good faith. That good faith must not be betrayed. Institutions of constitutional importance must never be politicised and weaponised to not honour the guarantees," he said.

The CJP spokesperson said the deadline for the government to honour its guarantees expires on Tuesday. "We once again call upon it to fulfil every commitment it made: withdraw the FIRs, ensure that no protester is subjected to future punitive action, and honour both the letter and the spirit of the assurance that brought an end to the protest."

He warned that if the guarantees are not honoured, the CJP will have "no option but to resume its nationwide protest." "A government that breaks its word cannot expect the youth to remain silent. If the guarantees are dishonoured, the streets of India will once again become the voice of its young," Das said.

The CJP had called off its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar on July 25 after the government accepted its key demands, including the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

World.title: Don't damage water bodies under garb of beautification: SC warns Bihar government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Taking a stern view of allegations that the Bihar government is filling parts of three historic ponds in Darbhanga to create public amenities such as recreation spaces and stalls, the Supreme Court on Tuesday warned the state govt ânot to touch the water bodies under the garb of beautificationâ without its approval.

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed the state govt to immediately stall the ongoing work related to the âBeautification and Rejuvenation of Gangasagar, Digghi and Harahi Lakeâ project. Although the state refuted the allegations of encroachment and urged the court to allow the work to continue, describing it as an ambitious project worth more than â¹100 crore, the bench refused to budge and ordered that no further work be carried out.

âYou cannot fill up water bodies under the garb of beautification. Do not touch the water ponds, keep your hands off and tell your officers not to touch the ponds,â the bench told advocate Manish Kumar, who was appearing for the state government.

TOI had reported on July 13, with photographs, that three ponds in Darbhanga were being filled with soil and boulders to make way for stalls and footpaths, despite strong opposition from local residents and environmentalists.





TOI report on Darbhanga ponds

Advocate Renu Prajapati, appearing for the Darbhanga-based voluntary group Talab Bachao Abhiyan (TBA), informed the bench that the three ponds form part of a list of protected wetlands and that any construction on their banks would violate rules and earlier rulings of the apex court. She also pointed out that the state, in its own affidavit, had admitted that around four acres of the ponds would be filled under the project.

In its affidavit, the state claimed that no arbitrary filling of the water bodies was taking place and that the activity was highly restricted and meticulously planned âEarth Filling & Stone Pitchingâ work.

âThis process is a necessity to stabilise and strengthen the severely eroded embankments, directly executing the mandate of the NGTâs order. Furthermore, the soil-filling footprint is strictly limited â for instance, constituting exactly 1.00 acre out of the 37.73-acre Harahi site, 1.42 acres out of the 50.97 acres at Digghi Lake, and 1.69 acres out of 44.22 acres at Gangasagar Lake,â the affidavit stated.

After a brief hearing, the bench directed the government to stop the work and ensure that the area of the ponds remain intact and is not reduced by filling..

Justifying the project, the state said the integration of public amenities is aimed at managing footfall, ensuring public hygiene, and preventing future degradation.

The court was hearing a plea filed by retired academicians, environmentalists and concerned citizens under the banner of TBA.

They are seeking urgent intervention to halt the filling of three historic ponds in Darbhanga â all 800â900 years old and integral to the cityâs identity.

âSince the State is acting in contravention of these orders and having been left with no other remedy, the petitioner herein is constrained to approach this court seeking an urgent and immediate remedy to stop further filling of the ponds and further to remove all the encroachments in and around the three ponds of Darbhanga and restore those to their original position as depicted in the maps of the years 1868 and 1960,â the petition stated.

In its response, the state submitted: âIt is respectfully submitted that in order to tackle the unregulated access which historically led to the lakes becoming open garbage dumps, the project provides structured and safe public utility interfaces including the construction of 11 designated bathing ghats equipped with 5 changing rooms and 7 sanitary toilet blocks to eliminate open defecation and water contamination.

â

World.title: As Maldives president seeks SAARC summit, India says cooperation requires goodwill
World.content:
With Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu calling for resumption of the biennial SAARC summit process, India reiterated Tuesday that it's Pakistan's support for cross-border terrorism that has blocked the intergovernmental organisation, which was conceived to build a connected and integrated South Asia.

Muizzu in his Independence Day speech had also offered to act as a mediator between India and Pakistan to advance talks for an early leaders' summit.

The last SAARC summit was held in 2014 in Nepal. The next summit that Pakistan was scheduled to host in 2016 could never take place as India pulled out because of the cross-border Uri terrorist attack. India has since maintained that regional cooperation under SAARC is adversely affected due to continued support to cross-border terrorism and interference in the internal affairs of member-states by Pakistan.

Member-states like the Maldives, Bangladesh and Nepal have from time-to-time sought revival of the summit. "India favors strong regional cooperation and has been working towards it for several decades. Everyone in South Asia is aware of which country and what activities are responsible for stymieing SAARC," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, adding that cooperation requires goodwill.

The official was responding to a question about Muizzu's remarks in which he had sought "reactivation' of SAARC calling it vital for regional peace and security.





"We must bring matters to the point where the leaders of SAARC resume holding summits once again," said Muizzu.

"To those parties among whom differences have arisen in this regard, the Maldives calls upon you to set those matters aside, to prioritise friendship for the sake of regional development and regional peace, and to come to the negotiating table. Should the task prove challenging, the Maldives stands ready to take the initiative and act as a mediator to advance those discussions," said the president, adding that SAARC must be operationalised once again and that his administration would always champion peace.

Muizzu also said that SAARC had brought numerous benefits to the region

"However, we now witness a span of some nine years during which this organisation has been rendered, or has become, dysfunctional. Given that the foreign policy of the Maldives is structured...upon the principle that differences should be addressed through consultation, by bringing concerns to the discussion table, reaching resolutions, and moving forward in a manner that benefits all, the reactivation of SAARC is equally vital for regional peace and security," he added.

Muizzu said his government's foreign policy was based on the conviction that if differences are left to be settled by violence and force, no resolution will ever be found.

World.title: Demand for MSP, reforms: Protesting farmers breach police barricades enroute to Bhopal
World.content:
Farmers march from Narmadapuram to Bhopal (ANI image)

Farmers marching from Narmadapuram to Bhopal demanding 100 per cent procurement of moong at the Minimum Support Price (MSP) breached police barricades on Tuesday as they entered the Madhya Pradesh capital, intensifying their protest against the state government.Visuals from Bhopal showed farmers crossing police barricades while carrying the Tricolour. Police did not use force and eventually opened the route, allowing the farmers to proceed into the city.The protest, organised under the banner of the Samyukta Kisan Morcha, began on Monday with a sit-in at Sethanighat in Narmadapuram, where farmers recited the Hanuman Chalisa before starting their march towards Bhopal, PTI reported.Earlier, police had attempted to stop the march by erecting barricades at Bhopal Tiraha and other locations. District Magistrate Somesh Mishra and Superintendent of Police Saikrishna S. Thota held talks with the protesting farmers on National Highway-69, but the discussions failed to break the deadlock.The farmers are demanding 100 per cent procurement of moong under MSP, a solution to issues related to the e-token system, and the timely availability of fertilisers at reasonable prices.

World.title: 'Clock it', 'delulu': How Gen Z lingo took over Parliament during anti-paper leak Bill debate
World.content:
Parliament debates anti-paper leak Bill

'Clock it'

NDA MP's 'delulu' jibe at opposition

Priyanka's swipe at PM's videos

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 on Tuesday wasn't just about examination reforms and paper leaks. It also turned into an unexpected showcase of Gen Z vocabulary, with MPs across party lines dropping terms such as "clock it", "MIA", "FOMO" and "delulu" to sharpen their political arguments.From the treasury benches praising the Centre's reforms to the opposition attacking the government's handling of the NEET controversy, lawmakers reached for internet slang more commonly found on social media than in Parliament.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj used the Gen Z phrase "clock it" â a slang term used to recognise something â while backing the proposed legislation.Speaking in favour of the Bill, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution."Calling the amendment a "transformative" step, Swaraj argued that it reflected the government's commitment to protecting the integrity of public examinations."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government.Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Lata Eknath Shinde turned to multiple Gen Z expressions to mock the opposition's protests over the NEET paper leak."I'd like to sum up the opposition's protest in Gen Z language. They were MIA (missing in action) for the first 37 days and did not go to Jantar Mantar. Then came FOMO (fear of missing out), so they held a protest outside the Prime Minister's residence. Finally, they became 'delulu' (delusional), believing the protesting students would join themâbut no one did," Shinde said.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, meanwhile, invoked Gen Z while targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public outreach, arguing that young people could see through political messaging."If you want to win over the Gen Z, then making videos with different camera angles will not help. The prime minister needs to change the angle of his heart, not the angle of cameras," she said.She also urged the government to acknowledge the concerns raised by students over the examination controversy."Injustice has been done with youths under your government, accept the truth. Prime Minister Narendra Modi must take responsibility," Priyanka said.The Lok Sabha began discussing the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill at 2pm on Tuesday. Union Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said leaders from several parties, including the Congress, Samajwadi Party, DMK and NCP, had agreed to extend the debate from the originally scheduled six hours to eight hours.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 7 LIVE: Student protest shattered BJP's 'Hindu-Muslim' narratives, says AAP MP
World.content:
Ending a week-long logjam, the Lok Sabha on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) began a discussion on the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, with Union Minister Jitendra Singh describing it as a reaffirmation of the government’s commitment to safeguard the welfare of students and the youth.

Also read | Opposition MPs seek apology from Amit Shah

Speaker Om Birla had announced in the Lok Sabha that he has allocated six hours for the debate on the Bill and if necessary, more time can be given based on the sense of the House. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the Opposition parties requested for two more hours (a total of eight hours), but further the government is willing to agree for a discussion of 10 hours in the Lok Sabha.

What is the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill | Explained

Meanwhile, the Rajya Sabha was adjourned for the day, shortly after the introduction of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026. A scheduled discussion on the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was not taken up. The Opposition refused to relent from its demand of seeking response from the government over police action on the student protesters in the national capital and other parts of the country.

World.title: Kochi Corporation among communicable disease hotspots
World.content:
The Health department has identified the Kochi Corporation and a few neighbouring local bodies as hotspots for several communicable diseases.

As many as 83 dengue cases, 10 typhoid cases, 11 leptospirosis cases, 78 hepatitis A cases, 55 Influenza A cases, and 26 H1N1 cases were reported within the Corporation limits alone. The figures cover the period from January to June 2026.

A senior Health official said advisories had been issued urging people to remain vigilant against the spread of diseases. Programmes would also be organised for medical professionals to respond promptly to H1N1 and leptospirosis cases.

The district recorded nine deaths due to leptospirosis in July.

The other local bodies that have been reported as hotspots for multiple diseases are Kalamassery, Thrikkakkara, Thripunithura, and Kadungalloor.

Kadungalloor reported 13 dengue cases, two cases each of leptospirosis and typhoid, 163 hepatitis A cases, eight Influenza A cases, and 10 H1N1 cases. Kalamassery reported 45 dengue cases, five Influenza A cases, 39 hepatitis A cases, and three cases each of leptospirosis and typhoid. The number of typhoid cases in Thrikkakkara stood at four, hepatitis A at 12, Influenza A at 24, and dengue at 23. Meanwhile, Thripunithura recorded 30 dengue cases and 15 H1N1 cases.

With the district witnessing a jump in infectious diseases during the past two months, efforts are on to curb their spread by intensifying precautionary measures. The Health department and the district panchayat have charted out an epidemic prevention action plan to be implemented across local bodies in the district.

Kochi Corporation health standing committee chairperson Seena Gokulan said the reports of hotspots were being regularly shared by the Health department, and that awareness programmes and intensive measures were being adopted to prevent the spread of diseases.

“Recently, we observed that some areas of Edappally, Ponnurunni, and Chambakkara reported a rise in dengue cases. Intensive source-reduction activities are being taken up to eliminate mosquitoes. We are carrying out spraying and fogging activities while also targeting areas with high incidences of diseases to prevent outbreaks. Awareness campaigns are also being organised. Intensive precautionary measures are taken in association with the Health department,” said Ms. Gokulan.

She added that one of the major sources of mosquito breeding was water collected in indoor plant pots, and that the public should be aware of it and ensure that they do not create breeding grounds for mosquitoes.

World.title: ADGP M.R. Ajith Kumar challenges his suspension before Central Administrative Tribunal
World.content:
The suspended Additional Director General of Police (ADGP) M.R. Ajith Kumar complained that he was suspended from service with the malafide intention of excluding him from being considered for the upcoming post of the Director General of Police (DGP).

In his petition filed before the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Mr. Ajith Kumar contended that he was suspended from service seven days prior to him being considered for the promotion to negate his legitimate right to get promoted as the DGP. The suspension order issued by the Chief Secretary was without any jurisdiction, he argued.

The CAT, which refused to grant a stay on the suspension order, posted the case for August 20, 2026.

The Chief Secretary had suspended him based on a report that he had deliberately interfered with the investigation and forced a referral report regarding the police case booked in connection with the alleged act of the members of the Permanent Escort and Security Team of the then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, who got out from the escort vehicles with lathis and assaulted the Youth Congress workers who protested while a bus carrying Mr. Vijayan and his Cabinet colleagues was passing through during the Nava Kerala Sadas Yatra on December 15, 2023.

Mr. Ajith Kumar, who was represented by Girija Gopal, argued that the report of the Special Investigation Team (SIT), which was relied on by the government to suspend him, appeared to be a conscious and deliberate attempt to fix responsibility on him and to make it appear that he had deliberately changed the conclusions and filed a refer report in the case.

The official had specifically denied any involvement on his part in the alleged act of filing the refer report.

He further argued that the attempt of the SIT to impute on the applicant the responsibility for filing the closure report in the case was totally ill-motivated and beyond the scope of investigation of the team.

The suspension based on the letter by the State Police Chief stating that the explanation given was not fully satisfactory cannot be legally sustained, he argued.

The senior police officer pointed out that he was due to retire in 2028 and any delay or denial of promotion as DGP on the purported grounds of the suspension order, which was issued in the nick of time when he was due to be promoted, would cause him inexplicable injury.

World.title: Delhi Police attempted to arrest Aishe Ghosh, alleges SFI
World.content:
The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) alleged that the Delhi police attempted to arrest its national joint secretary Aishe Ghosh, one of the prominent faces of the recently concluded Jantar Mantar protest, in connection with a 2021 protest case.

The SFI, the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], stated that its members resisted the arrest when the police barged into the party office at the AKG Bhavan. The police later left without taking her into custody.

“SFI national joint secretary Aishe, who was one of the leading student leaders of the recent wave of protests that resulted in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, is being subjected to witch-hunting by the Delhi police,” the SFI said in a statement.

According to Sachin Sharma, Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi), a local court had issued a non-bailable warrant against Ms. Ghosh in connection with the 2021 case after she failed to appear on multiple occasions. The next date of hearing is July 30. “We were only following the court’s orders,” he said, without revealing details of the case.

Delhi Police forcibly entered the CPI(M) Headquarters, AKG Bhavan, in an attempt to arrest SFI leader @aishe_ghosh.

The illegal attempt was firmly resisted by CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP @JohnBrittas, who forcefully intervened to stop the police from carrying out this unlawful action. pic.twitter.com/PMr1jgxsmn — CPI (M) (@cpimspeak) July 28, 2026

Earlier, speaking to mediapersons, CPI(M) MP John Brittas said, “Today, Delhi Police officers barged into the office of the CPI(M), which is a national party. They wanted to take Aishe Ghosh into custody. She was one of the faces of the Jantar Mantar agitation. They say that there is a warrant against her, which relates to a 2021 case.”

He added, “I checked with the police, and they said that a warrant had been issued against her. The warrant was communicated over the phone. You cannot communicate a warrant over the telephone; it should be personally handed over. Now, they intend to send a message to all students who participated in the agitation.”

Leader of Opposition in the Kerala Assembly and former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan said that the police had attempted to “forcibly enter the CPI(M) Central Committee office” to arrest Ms. Ghosh, in the wake of the SFI’s active participation in the Jantar Mantar protest.

He said, “Such blatant misuse of power reflects the BJP-led Union government’s growing intolerance of dissent. This is a moment for everyone who believes in democracy to speak out. Attempts to intimidate and criminalise dissent must be resisted, and the constitutional right to protest must be defended.”

World.title: Akhilesh Yadav compares police action at Delhi protest to Emergency, says Pradhan’s exit saved PM
World.content:
Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) compared the police action against students protesting the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test-Undergraduate (NEET-UG) paper leak with the Emergency, and claimed the Narendra Modi government had been forced to bend before an unprecedented student movement.

Also read | Public examinations amendment Bill does not address fundamental issues: AISEC

The resignation of former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan reflected the pressure generated by the student agitation, Mr. Yadav said, participating in the Lok Sabha debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.

“By removing one ‘Pradhan’, you effectively saved the ‘Pradhan Mantri’,” the SP leader said, adding that the government had abandoned its “arrogance” after students compelled it to accept their demands.

Calling the NEET-UG protests the first student agitation to receive the active backing of parents, Mr. Yadav said the government was “rattled” and had no option but to bow before the protesters. The police used “lathis with spikes, and electric batons” against students, describing the scenes in Delhi as reminiscent of the Emergency, he alleged.

When Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju countered that a government responding to protests was preferable to one imposing the Emergency, Mr. Yadav replied that while he had not witnessed the Emergency, “we have seen echoes of it in the national capital”.

Mr. Yadav also questioned the effectiveness of the proposed amendments, arguing that examination paper leaks continued despite existing laws. He took a swipe at the government over the outsourcing of the National Testing Agency and said the Opposition feared that “the entire government could be outsourced”.

The SP chief also targeted the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) over chadhawa chori (donation theft) at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya during the debate.

World.title: Mariners, families seek protection amid West Asia conflict
World.content:
Philip Mathews, 68, who left his seafaring career 34 years ago after serving as a captain, says he no longer recognises the waters he once sailed.

His seafaring career began in 1978, when he was just 20, with the Shipping Corporation of India. He left the service in 1992 to start a shipping company in Kochi.

“Back then, seafaring was among the safest and most peaceful of careers. Then pirates appeared on the scene, targeting ships off Somalia and West Asia. The latest West Asia conflict has escalated the risks manifold. How are mariners supposed to deal with bombs and missiles?” Mr. Mathews asked. He stressed that governments must ensure compliance with guidelines laid down by global organisations such as the International Maritime Organisation, International Trade Federation, and the International Labour Organisation.

He was among the 150-odd active seafarers and families of mariners who staged a silent march under the aegis of the Mariners Society, Ernakulam, protesting the killing of seafarers in military action. They also held a candlelight vigil against the ongoing West Asia war, demanding that mariners not be made collateral damage. “War has no place at sea,” “Protect seafarer, protect trade,” and “Safe passage is a human right,” read some of the placards held aloft during the march.

Captain Sardar Kandathil, 59, an active sailor for the last three decades, said that among the many hardships facing mariners are difficulties in going ashore at various destinations, including the Persian Gulf, and joining duty on time due to increasingly complicated visa regulations. “The biggest threat, though, is the free fall in job opportunities caused by the volatile situation in the maritime sector. It threatens to sabotage India’s vision of becoming a global maritime power, despite substantial investments in shipbuilding and maritime training institutions to groom potential mariners, including many women cadets,” he rued.

Mr. Kandathil pointed out that the Director General of Shipping’s circular warning Indian seafarers against sailing through the Strait of Hormuz has ended up benefiting counterparts from countries such as China and Indonesia. “Those nations are facilitating their mariners, and this will eventually lead to long-term job losses for Indian seafarers,” he said.

Benny Kollassany, secretary of the Mariners Society and a former mariner with 36 years of experience, said the organisation had submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister and would forward it to the Union government shortly. “India should leverage its market potential to take the initiative in ending the West Asia conflict. The prolonged conflict has driven up the prices of goods well beyond oil and gas,” he said.

T. Jayanchandran, whose son is currently on duty aboard a ship in Vietnam, said families of mariners live in a state of perpetual fear due to the conflict. “Many families are also dependent on the earnings of seafarers, who are often the sole breadwinners,” he said.

World.title: Kerala police intensify probe into loan app racket targeting American citizens; hunt on for kingpin
World.content:
A day after stumbling upon a sophisticated international loan app racket that operated from a makeshift call centre in Sreekaryam, the Thiruvananthapuram City police have gathered further information regarding the syndicate that primarily targeted foreign nationals.

The operation, which functioned under the guise of an IT company at a rented office at Chenthi, was unearthed during a raid conducted as part of the anti-drug enforcement drive Operation Toofan on Monday.

While nearly 20 people were apprehended during the operation, 13 employees, all natives of northern India, have been arrested. The seized items include 41 computers along with several digital storage devices and other electronic equipment.

According to official sources, the gang focused on foreign victims, particularly American citizens, and there is no evidence thus far that Indians were targeted through the operation. The investigators are examining the digital evidence to determine the scale of the fraud. The group’s bank accounts are also being scrutinised to assess the total value of financial transactions.

Investigators point out that the call centre is found to have operated through the night until the early hours of the morning in order to match the working hours in the United States and other foreign countries. The fraud began with victims receiving messages falsely claiming that their loan applications had already been approved. Those who responded were asked to provide personal and financial details, which were then forwarded to the alleged mastermind, who has been identified as Akashdeep Choudary, a Gujarat native.

According to preliminary investigation, the suspect previously operated from a different base in Ulloor before relocating to Sreekaryam. With the accused escaping prior to the raid, the police have issued a lookout notice to bring him to book. Another suspect has been apprehended from the Ahmedabad airport.

The racket offered its employees monthly salaries ranging ₹10,000 to ₹15,000. The staff members were also paid ₹1000 as commission for every victim who is successfully persuaded to enter the fraudulent loan process, sources said.

World.title: Three construction workers trapped in landslip in Kerala’s Kasaragod rescued
World.content:
Three construction workers were trapped in a roadside landslip at Kothankara near Cheruvathur in Kasaragod on Tuesday afternoon (July 28) as heavy rain triggered the collapse of earth onto a house construction site. They were later rescued and shifted to a private hospital at Cheruvathur. None of them is reported to be seriously injured.

The incident occurred around noon when a portion of the roadside embankment caved in, burying the workers who were engaged in the construction of a house near the road.

The injured are Ashokan and Vijesh of Karivellur and Ashokan of Maniyat.

Eyewitnesses said the workers were buried up to their necks under the debris. Residents rushed to the spot and began rescue efforts before personnel from the Fire and Rescue Services from Cheemeni and Nadakavu arrived and took over the operation.

Rescue teams worked cautiously to extricate the trapped workers safely as there was a risk of further landslip due to the continuing rain. Following several hours of effort, the workers were safely pulled out from the debris and taken to hospital.

Meanwhile, the authorities have urged residents to remain vigilant as heavy rain continues in the area.

World.title: India curtails 8,133 GWh of solar power as grid struggles to absorb excess daytime supply
World.content:
During April-June, when the country’s peak power demand touched a record high of 270 gigawatts (GW), the grid operators had to curtail 8,133 gigawatt-hour (GWh) of electricity generated by solar power sources due to transmission bottlenecks and to maintain grid security, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) informed the Parliament on Tuesday.



The curtailed electricity from solar sources is approximately equal to one-and-a-half days’ worth of power consumed by the entire country in April-June.

Solar power curtailment stood at 2,417 GWh in April, rising to 3,235 GWh in May and ⁠was at 2,481 GWh in June, the ministry said. “Renewable energy curtailment is implemented for reliable and secure operation of the grid,” it added.

World.title: Italy turn back to Roberto Mancini to end World Cup exile
World.content:
Roberto Mancini has returned for a second spell as Italy’s manager while Claudio Ranieri will be technical director, the country’s football president told reporters on Tuesday. Mancini replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who left in April after Italy failed to secure qualification to the 2026 FIFA World Cup, an unprecedented third consecutive time that the four-time champions had failed to make it to the marquee tournament.



“Mancini is the coach,” said Italian Football Federation (FIGC) President Giovanni Malago before confirming ?the decision at a press conference. “I believed that the best person to become head coach was Roberto Mancini,” Malago ?told reporters.

Mancini, who had 36 caps for Italy in his playing career, previously managed the team between 2018 and 2023, taking over when they failed to qualify for the World Cup for the first time since 1958 under Gian Piero Ventura. Italy then failed to qualify again under Mancini for the 2022 tournament. At Mancini club level has managed Inter Milan, Fiorentina and Manchester City, where he spent three years and guided them to their first Premier League title in 2011-12.

World.title: 6 incredible coastal airports you should see at least once
World.content:
Most airports are surrounded by highways, fields or cityscapes. But in some parts of the world, runways sit on narrow islands, reclaimed land or right beside the sea because coastal regions often have little flat land to build on. The result? Aircraft that skim over turquoise waters, beaches where planes become tourist attractions, and some of the most breathtaking take-offs and landings you’ll ever see.



1. Princess Juliana International Airport, Sint Maarten

Perhaps the world’s most famous coastal airport, Princess Juliana International Airport is known for its dramatic approaches over Maho Beach. Aircraft fly incredibly low over beachgoers before touching down just beyond the shoreline. Watching the landings has become one of the Caribbean island’s biggest tourist attractions. However, authorities warn visitors to stay behind safety barriers, as the powerful jet blast from departing aircraft can be dangerous.

World.title: Pune’s SPPU employee accused of selling fake degree for Rs 3 lakh, probe launched
World.content:
The Savitribai Phule Pune University launched a probe after allegations surfaced that an employee from the finance and accounts department sold a fake degree in exchange for Rs 3 lakh to a rickshaw driver’s son.

Mahesh Kadam, a rickshaw driver, visited SPPU to enquire about his son’s higher education, when Ramesh Mukhekar, an official from the Finance and Accounts Department, with his accomplices agreed to provide a BCom degree certificate to Kadam for Rs 3 lakh.

However, the certificates Kadam received bore the name “University of Pune” instead of “Savitribai Phule Pune University”. He also alleged that four different degree certificates were awarded for four years of study. A written complaint was filed with the Vice Chancellor’s office.

World.title: ‘I was trembling’: Kajal Aggarwal recalls assistant director removing shirt to show tattoo
World.content:
Kajal Aggarwal has been one of South India’s most adored stars for nearly two decades, inspiring an immense fan following across languages. But the actor says one fan encounter on a film set left her shaken rather than flattered.

In an interview with ABP News, Kajal opened up about an unsettling incident involving an assistant director who entered her caravan without permission while she was alone and surprised her by revealing a tattoo of her name. While she appreciated the gesture, she said the way it unfolded crossed a line.

Kajal Aggarwal recalls unsettling incident

Recalling the incident, Kajal said, “A few days ago, after wrapping up a shoot for a film, I was resting in my caravan. At that time, a person working as an assistant director on the film suddenly entered my caravan without taking permission. He immediately took off his shirt and showed me a tattoo of my name on his chest. I was so shocked by the incident that my hands and legs started trembling.”

World.title: Nirav Modi to be deported once legal proceedings conclude: MEA
World.content:
Nirav Modi is wanted in India to stand trial on fraud and money laundering charges in a $2 billion Punjab National Bank loan scam case.

RESPONDING TO reports about former British Home Secretary Priti Patel’s claims that New Delhi has refused to take back thousands of illegal Indian migrants from the UK because London has not extradited Nirav Modi, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Tuesday said that there is a set procedure followed for the deportation of any person, and that paperwork is undertaken to establish citizenship.

“The legal proceedings against Nirav Modi are underway, and he will be deported once these proceedings conclude,” said Randhir Jaiswal, MEA’s official spokesperson. He reiterated that the Indian government remains “committed to bringing the fugitive offender back” to face due legal process.

World.title: Embolo’s red vs Argentina in World Cup quarterfinal wrong, says IFAB
World.content:
Referee Joao Pinheiro, of Portugal, gives a red card for Switzerland's Breel Embolo (7) during the World Cup quarterfinal soccer match between Argentina and Switzerland in Kansas City, Mo., Saturday, July 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Ed Zurga)

The controversy around Argentina matches refuses to die down even after the end of the World Cup almost one and a half weeks ago with football’s law-making body IFAB on Tuesday saying that Switzerland’s Breel Embolo should not have been sent off during the quarter-final against the La Albiceleste.

Embolo had received a second yellow card during the second half with the match level at 1-1. Argentina struck twice in extra ⁠time ​to beat 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in Kansas City. The 29-year-old had gone down following a challenge by Leandro Paredes, and referee Joao Pinheiro initially booked the Argentina midfielder. But ​the ​VAR informed the referee that Paredes ⁠had not committed a foul, and Pinheiro booked Embolo instead for simulation.

World.title: Held after massive search, TET leak key accused taken to Bihar to recover evidence: police
World.content:
The Special Investigation Team, probing the Maharashtra Teachers Eligibility Test (TET) paper leak, on Monday took the key accused of the case, Bijendra Gupta, to Bihar to verify certain facts and recover evidence believed to be linked to the conspiracy.

Gupta was arrested from Bihar last week after he was on the run for over three weeks, constantly shifting between Delhi, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh while avoiding all direct contact with his family in a calculated attempt to evade arrest.

Despite frequently changing locations and relying on intermediaries to communicate, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) managed to tracked him down by deploying 75 police personnel in four states after a massive search using advanced surveillance techniques.

World.title: Militant elements within proscribed JAAC protests pursuing foreign agenda: Tarar
World.content:
Referring to the recent violence in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Tuesday said the protests by the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) were not peaceful but violent, alleging that militant elements pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding were involved.

‘Fitna Al Khawarij elements present among protesters’

Earlier today, AJK Information Secretary Muhammad Rashid Hanif claimed that a significant number of protesters participating in the proscribed JAAC demonstration in AJK were affiliated with Fitna Al Khawarij.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

Addressing a press conference, Hanif said that illegal and violent activities had taken place in AJK aimed at disrupting the upcoming phases of elections in the region.

“The fundamental duty of the state is to maintain law and order, continue the democratic process and fulfil this responsibility. The state is capable of doing so,” he stressed.

The senior official reiterated that the JAAC protest included individuals linked to Fitna Al Khawarij rather than only ordinary citizens.

He also played a video as evidence, which showed masked gunmen on the roof of a building in the region.

“Common people are fewer in number; however, armed individuals, militants and Fitna Al Khawarij members are present, which falls under the definition of terrorism,” Hanif maintained.

“They have involved innocent people by misleading them. We appeal to the people to distance themselves from them. The government will also make some public announcements in this regard to fulfil its responsibility,” he stated.

The regional information secretary added that anti-state elements were using children and women as human shields.

“Several misleading videos have also been circulated on social media, indicating that it is a human rights movement; however, that is not the case.”

Hanif said that state institutions had adequate information regarding the presence of Fitna Al Khawarij elements and members of other militant organisations.

Addressing the media after the information secretary, AJK police spokesperson and Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Irfan Kashfi said that such elements would be “handled in the same way that any terrorists or militants are handled”.

He said that their possession of modern weapons and resources — including automatic weapons, M-4 rifles, SMGs, AK-47s and, according to initial information, even sniper weapons — showed that they were “not peaceful protesters, but militants”.

The DIG said one police official had been martyred in the skirmishes, while five others were injured. He added that one suspect had been arrested in Rawalakot, from whose possession a military-grade weapon was recovered.

Citing initial information, Kashfi said the suspect was a foreign national who had been acting as a sniper.

“Security forces are answering [attacks] in self-defence and for the protection of the public,” Kashfi said, noting that law enforcement agencies have shown great endurance.

He added that facilitators of these militants were also being investigated.

The senior police official assured that there was no need to believe the “misconception” that these militants could capture Rawalakot or any other area, as LEAs would “persist at all costs”.

Earlier today, while sharing a video of several people carrying arms in AJK, the region’s Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore said, “They planned this for weeks and now they have got what they wanted: the blood of innocent Kashmiris.”

“The rioters not only have sophisticated weapons, they also have the advantage of access to all vantage points from where they take aim at security forces, whose only objective has been to contain the situation and prevent escalation,” Rathore stated.

He added that the march to Muzaffarabad during the elections was a “conniving plan to trigger mass unrest”.

“I appeal to the people to stay away from these agitators who have a proven record of using civilians as human shields and creating a win-win situation for themselves once security personnel act in self-defence,” he said.

Over the past month, the regional administration and the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly, which has resulted in protests across the region.

On June 5, the JAAC was declared a proscribed organisation by the regional government and placed under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA).

World.title: Coalition partners PPP, PML-N spar after first phase of AJK elections as political temperatures rise
World.content:
The PPP and the PML-N, coalition partners in the Centre, traded barbs on Tuesday after the conclusion of the first phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), with Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s party alleging rigging in the polls and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz urging it to accept defeat.

The PML-N grabbed nine out of the 13 constituencies of AJK’s Mirpur division in yesterday’s elections, preliminary results issued by the Election Commission showed.

Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on Monday. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polling process, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice.

In a televised statement, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz hailed the “outstanding victory” of the PML-N in the first phase of the AJK elections, urging the PPP to accept defeat.

“The PPP should have accepted its defeat by affirming the spirit of democracy, but I felt aggrieved by the kind of words used by PPP leaders.”

“The state does not decide election results; only the people make this decision,” she said in response to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations.

She added that when the PPP secured a majority in Gilgit-Baltistan’s elections, the PML-N acknowledged it, congratulated it and offered it the opportunity to form the government.

“Now you are alleging rigging by the PML-N; when you won the GB election, there was no rigging there, but as you have lost the AJK election badly, you are now levelling rigging allegations,” CM Maryam said.

The provincial chief executive further said that the PPP should have worked on its performance, built its narrative and presented a programme for the people. “Neither did you have the narrative, nor the performance, nor a programme for the people of AJK or any record of your governance.”

The Punjab chief minister added that the “continuity” the PPP received in Sindh could never be achieved by any other party. “Despite this, you had no project to show from Sindh; you could not tell [people about] your performance and could not give a roadmap of the future to the people of AJK.”

“If you want to get votes, you cannot cry before the people; the people are much more aware these days.”

CM Maryam said that during its election speeches, the PPP leadership kept blaming the federal government; however, it had forgotten that the PPP had been in power in AJK for the past year.

“During the PPP’s tenure, conditions in AJK became worse. You could not control the situation, and now you are crying over rigging,” she alleged.
